# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

</details>



NicheCompass (**N**iche **I**dentification based on **C**ellular grap**H** **E**mbeddings of **COM**munication **P**rograms **A**ligned across **S**patial **S**amples) is a Python package for end-to-end analysis of spatial multi-omics data. It focuses on spatial atlas building, niche identification, cell-cell communication inference, and spatial reference mapping. This document provides a high-level overview of the system architecture, core components, and key capabilities of NicheCompass.

Sources: [README.md:11-11](), [docs/index.md:3-4]()

## System Purpose and Scope

NicheCompass enables the comprehensive analysis of spatial transcriptomics and multi-modal omics data through:

1. **Spatial Data Processing**: Loading and preprocessing spatial omics data
2. **Gene Program Extraction**: Creating interpretable gene programs from biological databases
3. **Neural Network Modeling**: Using a Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder to learn cellular representations
4. **Niche Identification**: Identifying and characterizing cellular niches in spatial context
5. **Communication Analysis**: Inferring cell-cell communication networks
6. **Spatial Reference Mapping**: Aligning and integrating multiple spatial samples

The package is developed and maintained by the Lotfollahi Lab at the Wellcome Sanger Institute.

Sources: [README.md:11-11](), [docs/index.md:3-4]()

## High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NicheCompass Package"] --> B["Core Model System"]
    A --> C["Data Processing System"]
    A --> D["Analysis Utilities"]
    A --> E["Benchmarking Tools"]
    
    B --> B1["Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder"]
    B --> B2["Training Pipeline"]
    
    C --> C1["Spatial Data Loading"]
    C --> C2["Gene Program Creation"]
    C --> C3["Multimodal Integration"]
    
    D --> D1["Cell Communication Analysis"]
    D --> D2["Visualization Tools"]
    D --> D3["Spatial Reference Mapping"]
    
    E --> E1["CLISIS Benchmarking"]
    E --> E2["Neighborhood Preservation Metrics"]
    
    subgraph "Primary Use Cases"
        UC1["Single Sample Analysis"]
        UC2["Sample Integration"]
        UC3["Spatial Reference Mapping"]
        UC4["Multimodal Analysis"]
    end
```

The NicheCompass system consists of four main subsystems that work together to provide comprehensive spatial omics analysis. The core model system includes the variational autoencoder and training pipeline, while the data processing system handles data loading, gene program creation, and multimodal integration. Analysis utilities and benchmarking tools enable downstream analysis and evaluation.

Sources: [README.md:11-11](), [pyproject.toml:29-37](), [pyproject.toml:67-74]()

## Core Model and Data Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Spatial Multi-omics Data"] --> B["Data Loading & Preprocessing"]
    B --> C["Spatial Graph Construction"]
    B --> D["Gene Program Extraction"]
    
    D --> D1["OmniPath\nLigand-Receptor"]
    D --> D2["NicheNet\nLigand-Target"]
    D --> D3["MEBOCOST\nEnzyme-Sensor"]
    D --> D4["CollecTRI\nTF Network"]
    
    D1 & D2 & D3 & D4 --> E["Combined Gene Program Dictionary"]
    E --> F["Add GP Masks to AnnData"]
    
    C --> G["NicheCompass Model"]
    F --> G
    
    G --> H["Trained Model"]
    H --> I1["Niche Identification"]
    H --> I2["Cell-Cell Communication"]
    H --> I3["Sample Integration"]
    
    subgraph "Optional Multimodal Processing"
        J["ATAC-seq Data"] --> K["Gene-Peak Mapping"]
        K --> L["Add Chromatin Accessibility Mask"]
        L --> G
    end
```

The NicheCompass workflow begins with spatial multi-omics data, which undergoes preprocessing and spatial graph construction. In parallel, gene programs are extracted from multiple biological databases (OmniPath, NicheNet, MEBOCOST, and CollecTRI) and combined into a gene program dictionary. These gene programs are added as masks to the AnnData object, which is then used to train the NicheCompass model. The trained model enables various downstream analyses, including niche identification, cell-cell communication inference, and sample integration. Optionally, ATAC-seq data can be integrated through gene-peak mapping.

Sources: [pyproject.toml:29-37](), [pyproject.toml:67-74](), [pyproject.toml:75-77]()

## Model Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Input: AnnData"] --> B["Encoder"]
    B --> C["Latent Representation"]
    C --> D["Decoder"]
    D --> E["Reconstructed Data"]
    
    subgraph "Encoder Components"
        B1["Graph Neural Network Layer"]
        B2["Variational Layer"]
        B1 --> B2
    end
    
    subgraph "Latent Space Organization"
        C1["Prior Gene Programs"]
        C2["De Novo Gene Programs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decoder Components"
        D1["Gene Expression Decoder"]
        D2["Graph Decoder"]
        D3["ATAC Decoder (Optional)"]
    end
    
    B --> B1
    B2 --> C
    C --> C1
    C --> C2
    C --> D
    D --> D1
    D --> D2
    D --> D3
```

The NicheCompass model follows a variational autoencoder architecture. The encoder processes the input AnnData object using a graph neural network layer followed by a variational layer to produce a latent representation. The latent space is organized into prior gene programs (derived from biological databases) and de novo gene programs (learned from the data). The decoder reconstructs gene expression data, the graph structure, and optionally ATAC-seq data from the latent representation.

Sources: [docs/user_guide/index.md:7-13]()

## Gene Program System

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["External Biological Databases"] --> B["Gene Program Extraction"]
    B --> C["OmniPath Ligand-Receptor"]
    B --> D["NicheNet Ligand-Target"]
    B --> E["MEBOCOST Enzyme-Sensor"]
    B --> F["CollecTRI TF-Target"]
    
    C & D & E & F --> G["Gene Program Dictionary"]
    G --> H["Add to AnnData Object"]
    
    H --> I["GP Targets Mask"]
    H --> J["GP Sources Mask"]
    
    subgraph "NicheCompass Model Processing"
        K["Graph Neural Network"]
        I --> K
        J --> K
        K --> L["Latent Space"]
        L --> M["Interpretable Gene Programs"]
    end
```

The Gene Program system is a key component of NicheCompass. Gene programs are extracted from multiple external biological databases (OmniPath, NicheNet, MEBOCOST, and CollecTRI) and combined into a gene program dictionary. This dictionary is added to the AnnData object as GP targets and sources masks. These masks inform the graph neural network during model training, resulting in interpretable gene programs in the latent space.

Sources: [pyproject.toml:29-37](), [docs/user_guide/index.md:7-13]()

## Analysis Capabilities

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Trained NicheCompass Model"] --> B["Latent Representation"]
    A --> C["Reconstructed Gene Expression"]
    A --> D["Reconstructed Graph"]
    
    B --> E["Niche Identification"]
    E --> F["Niche Characterization"]
    
    B --> G["Cell-Cell Communication Analysis"]
    G --> H["Communication Network"]
    
    B --> I["Spatial Reference Mapping"]
    
    subgraph "Analysis Functions"
        J1["create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()"]
        J2["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"]
        J3["compute_communication_gp_network()"]
        J4["visualize_communication_gp_network()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Benchmarking Metrics"
        K1["CLISIS"]
        K2["Cell type Adjacency Score"]
        K3["Graph Connectivity Score"]
        K4["Neighborhood Preservation"]
    end
```

NicheCompass provides a variety of analysis capabilities for extracting insights from trained models. The latent representation enables niche identification and characterization, cell-cell communication analysis, and spatial reference mapping. The package includes functions for creating cell type chord plots, generating enriched gene program information plots, computing communication gene program networks, and visualizing these networks. Benchmarking metrics such as CLISIS, cell type adjacency score, graph connectivity score, and neighborhood preservation are available for evaluating model performance.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:22-1148]()

## Use Cases and Installation

NicheCompass supports several key use cases:

1. **Single Sample Analysis**: Analyzing a single spatial transcriptomics sample
2. **Sample Integration**: Integrating multiple spatial samples
3. **Spatial Reference Mapping**: Mapping across reference samples
4. **Multimodal Analysis**: Analyzing combined RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data

The package can be installed via pip:

```bash
pip install nichecompass
```

For more comprehensive installations with additional features:

```bash
# For benchmarking capabilities
pip install nichecompass[benchmarking]

# For multimodal analysis
pip install nichecompass[multimodal]

# For all features
pip install nichecompass[all]
```

For detailed tutorials and usage examples, refer to the [Tutorials](#4) section.

Sources: [README.md:13-16](), [pyproject.toml:67-74](), [pyproject.toml:75-77]()

Sources: [docs/release_notes/index.md:7-44]()

## Dependencies and System Requirements

NicheCompass is built on several key dependencies:

| Dependency | Purpose |
|------------|---------|
| PyTorch Geometric (PyG) | Graph neural network operations |
| AnnData | Data structure for annotated data matrices |
| scanpy | Single-cell analysis in Python |
| OmniPath | Protein-protein interaction database |
| decoupler | Footprint analysis tools |
| mlflow | Experiment tracking |

The package requires Python 3.9 or higher and is primarily tested on Linux operating systems.

Sources: [pyproject.toml:29-37](), [pyproject.toml:9-11](), [pyproject.toml:21-28]()

This document provides a comprehensive overview of the NicheCompass system architecture, detailing its components, data flow, and module organization. It explains how the various parts of the system interact to enable end-to-end analysis of spatial multi-omics data, including spatial atlas building, niche identification, cell-cell communication inference, and spatial reference mapping.

For installation instructions, please refer to [Installation](#3), and for practical application examples, see [Tutorials](#4).

## System Overview

NicheCompass is built on a modular architecture that integrates several key components to analyze spatial transcriptomics and multimodal data.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Core Components"
        VGPGAE["Variational Gene\nProgram Graph\nAutoencoder"]
        GP["Gene Program\nSystem"]
        MM["Multimodal\nIntegration"]
        Train["Training\nPipeline"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Processing"
        DP["Data Preprocessing"]
        SGC["Spatial Graph\nConstruction"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Utilities"
        CCA["Cell-Cell\nCommunication Analysis"]
        NID["Niche\nIdentification"]
        SRM["Spatial Reference\nMapping"]
        VIS["Visualization\nTools"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Benchmarking"
        CLISIS["Cell Type Local\nInverse Simpson's\nIndex Similarity"]
        NPM["Neighborhood\nPreservation Metrics"]
    end
    
    DP --> SGC
    DP --> GP
    SGC --> VGPGAE
    GP --> VGPGAE
    MM --> VGPGAE
    VGPGAE --> Train
    Train --> CCA
    Train --> NID
    Train --> SRM
    Train --> VIS
    Train --> CLISIS
    Train --> NPM
```

Sources: [README.md:11-11](), [pyproject.toml:8-8](), [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:1-4](), [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py:1-7]()

## Core Components

The NicheCompass system is composed of four main components that work together to analyze spatial multi-omics data:

### 1. Model Component

At the heart of NicheCompass is the `NicheCompass` model class, which implements a Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE). This model:
- Learns latent representations of cells in their spatial context
- Uses gene program masks to guide the learning of interpretable representations
- Supports multimodal data integration (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq)
- Enables various downstream analyses like niche identification

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "NicheCompass Model"
        direction LR
        NC["NicheCompass Class"]
        VGPMOD["VGPGAE Module"]
        BMM["BaseModelMixin"]
        
        NC --> BMM
        NC --> VGPMOD
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Inputs"
        AD["AnnData\n(gene expression)"]
        ADATAC["AnnData_atac\n(optional)"]
        ADJ["Adjacency Matrix\n(spatial_connectivities)"]
        GPM["Gene Program Masks\n(targets, sources)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Outputs"
        LAT["Latent Representation\n(nichecompass_latent)"]
        RADJ["Reconstructed Adjacency\n(nichecompass_recon_connectivities)"]
        AGGW["Aggregation Weights\n(nichecompass_agg_weights)"]
    end
    
    AD --> NC
    ADATAC --> NC
    ADJ --> NC
    GPM --> NC
    
    NC --> LAT
    NC --> RADJ
    NC --> AGGW
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:24-581](), [src/nichecompass/modules/__init__.py]()

### 2. Gene Program System

The Gene Program System is responsible for creating and managing interpretable gene programs that serve as the basis for the model's latent representations:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "External Knowledge Databases"
        OP["OmniPath\n(Ligand-Receptor)"]
        NN["NicheNet\n(Ligand-Target)"]
        MB["MEBOCOST\n(Enzyme-Sensor)"]
        CT["CollecTRI\n(TF-Target)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Gene Program Extraction"
        EOP["extract_gp_dict_from_omnipath_lr_interactions()"]
        ENN["extract_gp_dict_from_nichenet_lrt_interactions()"]
        EMB["extract_gp_dict_from_mebocost_ms_interactions()"]
        ECT["extract_gp_dict_from_collectri_tf_network()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Gene Program Processing"
        FCGP["filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps()"]
        AGP["add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata()"]
    end
    
    OP --> EOP
    NN --> ENN
    MB --> EMB
    CT --> ECT
    
    EOP --> FCGP
    ENN --> FCGP
    EMB --> FCGP
    ECT --> FCGP
    
    FCGP --> AGP
    
    AGP --> ADATA["AnnData with GP Masks"]
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:286-356](), [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:359-596](), [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:599-665](), [src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py:11-18]()

```mermaid
    subgraph "Trainer"

        EP["Epoch Processing"]
        LM["Loss Monitoring"]
        BM["Best Model Selection"]
    end
    
    PD --> TI
    ID --> TI
    TI --> TR
    TR --> EP
    EP --> LM
    LM --> ES
    ES --> BM
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:28-91](), [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:217-306](), [src/nichecompass/data/__init__.py:1-6]()

NicheCompass provides a suite of utilities for analyzing the trained model results:


## Data Flow

NicheCompass processes data through a well-defined pipeline that integrates spatial information, gene expression, and prior biological knowledge:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Data"
        AD["AnnData\n(gene expression)"]
        ADJ["Spatial Adjacency\nMatrix"]
        ADATAC["AnnData_atac\n(optional)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Gene Programs"
        GPDB["External DB\nGene Programs"]
        ADDON["De Novo\nGene Programs"]
        GPM["Gene Program\nMasks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "NicheCompass Model"
        ENC["Encoder\n(GNN)"]
        LAT["Latent\nRepresentation"]
        DEC["Decoder\n(Gene Expression,\nGraph, ATAC)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output & Analysis"
        REC["Reconstructed\nData"]
        NID["Niche\nIdentification"]
        CCC["Cell-Cell\nCommunication"]
        SRM["Spatial Reference\nMapping"]
    end
    
    AD --> ENC
    ADJ --> ENC
    ADATAC --> ENC
    
    GPDB --> GPM
    ADDON --> GPM
    GPM --> ENC
    GPM --> DEC
    
    ENC --> LAT
    LAT --> DEC
    DEC --> REC
    
    LAT --> NID
    LAT --> CCC
    LAT --> SRM
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:189-249](), [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:91-166](), [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:18-111]()

## Code Organization

The NicheCompass codebase is organized into several modules, each handling specific aspects of the system:

| Module | Purpose | Key Classes/Functions |
|--------|---------|----------------------|
| `models` | Defines the main model class | `NicheCompass` |
| `modules` | Contains neural network components | `VGPGAE` |
| `nn` | Low-level neural network modules | - |
| `data` | Data loading and preprocessing | `SpatialAnnTorchDataset`, `initialize_dataloaders` |
| `train` | Training pipeline | `Trainer` |
| `utils` | Utility functions | Gene program extraction, analysis utilities |
| `benchmarking` | Evaluation metrics | `compute_clisis`, `compute_cas`, `compute_gcs` |

Sources: [src/nichecompass/__init__.py:3-5](), [pyproject.toml:30-37]()

## Model Architecture Details

The Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE) is the core model of NicheCompass:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Encoder"
        FC["Fully Connected\nLayers"]
        GNN["Graph Neural\nNetwork Layer"]
        VAR["Variational\nLayer"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Latent Space"
        PGP["Prior Gene\nPrograms"]
        DGP["De Novo Gene\nPrograms"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decoder"
        GED["Gene Expression\nDecoder"]
        GD["Graph\nDecoder"]
        AD["ATAC\nDecoder"]
    end
    
    Input["Input Data\n(Gene Expression,\nChromatin Accessibility)"] --> FC
    FC --> GNN
    GNN --> VAR
    VAR --> PGP
    VAR --> DGP
    
    PGP --> GED
    DGP --> GED
    PGP --> GD
    DGP --> GD
    PGP --> AD
    DGP --> AD
    
    GED --> GeneExpr["Reconstructed\nGene Expression"]
    GD --> Graph["Reconstructed\nGraph"]
    AD --> ATACExpr["Reconstructed\nChromatin Accessibility"]
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:547-581]()

## Configuration and Hyperparameters

NicheCompass provides several configuration options and hyperparameters that influence model performance:

| Parameter Category | Key Parameters | Description |
|--------------------|---------------|-------------|
| **Model Structure** | `n_fc_layers_encoder`, `n_layers_encoder`, `n_hidden_encoder` | Control the size and depth of the encoder network |
| | `conv_layer_encoder` | Type of GNN layer ("gcnconv" or "gatv2conv") |
| | `n_addon_gp` | Number of de novo gene programs to learn |
| **Loss Weights** | `lambda_edge_recon` | Weight for edge reconstruction loss |
| | `lambda_gene_expr_recon` | Weight for gene expression reconstruction loss |
| | `lambda_chrom_access_recon` | Weight for chromatin accessibility reconstruction loss |
| **Training Process** | `n_epochs`, `n_epochs_all_gps` | Control training duration and GP pruning timing |
| | `lr`, `weight_decay` | Control optimizer behavior |
| **Gene Program System** | `min_genes_per_gp`, `max_genes_per_gp` | Filter gene programs by size |
| | `active_gp_thresh_ratio` | Threshold for determining active gene programs |

Sources: [docs/user_guide/index.md:5-16](), [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:189-249](), [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:217-306]()

## Multimodal Integration

NicheCompass supports multimodal analysis of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "RNA Data"
        RNA["AnnData\n(RNA-seq)"]
        GPR["RNA Gene\nProgram Masks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ATAC Data"
        ATAC["AnnData\n(ATAC-seq)"]
        GPA["ATAC Gene\nProgram Masks"]
        GPM["Gene-Peak\nMapping"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integrated Model"
        ENC["Encoder"]
        LAT["Latent\nRepresentation"]
        DEC["Multimodal\nDecoder"]
    end
    
    RNA --> ENC
    ATAC --> ENC
    GPR --> ENC
    GPA --> ENC
    GPM --> DEC
    
    ENC --> LAT
    LAT --> DEC
    
    DEC --> RNARec["Reconstructed\nRNA"]
    DEC --> ATACRec["Reconstructed\nATAC"]
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:339-374](), [src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py:8-10]()

## Version and Dependency Management

NicheCompass is meticulously versioned and has specific dependencies that ensure its functionality:

| Dependency Category | Key Dependencies | Purpose |
|---------------------|-----------------|---------|
| **Core Dependencies** | PyTorch Geometric (PyG) | Graph neural network framework |
| | AnnData | Data structure for annotated data matrices |
| | scanpy | Single-cell analysis in Python |
| | omnipath | Access to multiple databases of molecular biology |
| | decoupler | Tool for extraction of biological signatures |
| **Optional Dependencies** | scib-metrics | Benchmarking metrics |
| | squidpy | Spatial single-cell analysis |
| | scglue | For multimodal data integration |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:29-81](), [environment.yaml:8-14](), [docs/release_notes/index.md:7-44]()

## Conclusion

The NicheCompass architecture is designed to provide a comprehensive framework for spatial multi-omics data analysis. By integrating graph neural networks with interpretable gene programs and supporting multimodal data, it enables researchers to identify and characterize cellular niches, infer cell-cell communication, and map spatial references across samples.

The modular design allows for flexible analysis workflows and extension to different biological questions, while the core model ensures that the learned representations preserve both gene expression patterns and spatial relationships.

The Core Model of NicheCompass is the central analytical engine within the system, responsible for transforming spatial multi-omics data into a biologically interpretable latent space. This page documents the architecture, components, and functionality of the Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE), which forms the foundation of NicheCompass's analytical capabilities.

For information about how Gene Programs are created and used, see [Gene Programs](#2.2).
For information about multimodal integration, see [Multimodal Integration](#2.3).

## Architecture Overview

The Core Model follows a variational graph autoencoder architecture that has been specially designed to handle spatial omics data and incorporate prior biological knowledge through gene programs.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Input: AnnData"] --> B["Encoder"]
    B --> C["Latent Representation"]
    C --> D["Decoders"]
    D --> E["Reconstructed Data"]
    
    subgraph "Encoder"
        B1["Graph Neural Network Layer"]
        B2["Variational Layer"]
        B1 --> B2
    end
    
    subgraph "Latent Space"
        C1["Prior Gene Programs"]
        C2["De Novo Gene Programs"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Decoders"
        D1["Gene Expression Decoder"]
        D2["Graph Decoder"]
        D3["ATAC Decoder (optional)"]
    end
```

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:778-791]()

## Key Components

### NicheCompass Model Class

The `NicheCompass` class serves as the primary interface to the Core Model, providing methods for initialization, training, and analysis:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class NicheCompass {
        +AnnData adata
        +AnnData adata_atac (optional)
        +VGPGAE model_
        +train()
        +get_latent_representation()
        +compute_differential_gps()
        +analyze_cell_cell_communication()
        +save()
        +load()
    }
    
    class VGPGAE {
        +Encoder encoder
        +GeneExpressionDecoder gene_expr_decoder
        +GraphDecoder graph_decoder
        +ChromatinAccessibilityDecoder chrom_access_decoder
        +forward()
        +get_active_gp_mask()
    }
    
    class Trainer {
        +train()
        +optimize_model()
        +early_stopping
    }
    
    NicheCompass *-- VGPGAE : contains
    NicheCompass --> Trainer : uses
```

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:24-219]()
- [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:28-166]()

### Variational Gene Program Graph Autoencoder (VGPGAE)

The VGPGAE is the mathematical core of NicheCompass, transforming spatial omics data into an interpretable latent space where each dimension corresponds to a gene program.

#### Encoder

The encoder processes input data through graph neural network layers and applies a variational transformation:

- **Graph Neural Network Layer**: Captures spatial relationships between cells
- **Variational Layer**: Produces a probabilistic latent representation by mapping to a distribution (mean μ and log variance logσ²)

The encoder architecture is configurable with parameters such as:
- `conv_layer_encoder`: Type of graph convolutional layer (e.g., GCNConv, GATv2Conv)
- `n_hidden_encoder`: Number of hidden nodes
- `n_layers_encoder`: Number of message passing layers

#### Latent Space

The latent space combines two types of gene programs:

- **Prior Gene Programs**: Based on known biological pathways (e.g., ligand-receptor interactions)
- **De Novo Gene Programs**: Learned from the data without prior constraints, enabling discovery of new patterns

#### Decoders

The model includes multiple decoders:

1. **Gene Expression Decoder**: Reconstructs gene expression data using linear masked layers that enforce the gene program structure
2. **Graph Decoder**: Reconstructs the spatial graph structure using cosine similarity
3. **Chromatin Accessibility Decoder** (optional): Reconstructs ATAC-seq data in multimodal analysis

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:189-219]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:885-896]()

## Data Flow

The following diagram illustrates how data flows through the Core Model:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["AnnData with
    Gene Expression + Spatial Info"] --> B["Create Gene Program Mask"]
    A1["AnnData with ATAC-seq (optional)"] --> B1["Create Chromatin 
    Accessibility Mask (optional)"]
    
    B --> C["Initialize Model"]
    B1 --> C
    
    C --> D["Train Model"]
    D --> E["Encoder"]
    E --> F["Latent Representation
    (Gene Programs)"]
    
    F --> G1["Gene Expression Decoder"]
    F --> G2["Graph Decoder"]
    F --> G3["ATAC Decoder (optional)"]
    
    G1 --> H1["Reconstructed Gene Expression"]
    G2 --> H2["Reconstructed Spatial Graph"]
    G3 --> H3["Reconstructed Chromatin Accessibility"]
    
    F --> I["Downstream Analysis
    (e.g., Cell-Cell Communication)"]
```

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:778-847]()

## Model Initialization and Training

### Initialization

The NicheCompass model is initialized with:

1. AnnData object containing gene expression and spatial information
2. Optional AnnData object with ATAC-seq data for multimodal analysis
3. Configuration parameters for model architecture and training

Example initialization from the mouse brain multimodal tutorial:

```python
model = NicheCompass(adata,
                     adata_atac,
                     counts_key="counts",
                     adj_key="spatial_connectivities",
                     gp_names_key="nichecompass_gp_names",
                     active_gp_names_key="nichecompass_active_gp_names",
                     gp_targets_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_targets",
                     gp_targets_categories_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_targets_categories",
                     gp_sources_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_sources",
                     gp_sources_categories_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_sources_categories",
                     latent_key="nichecompass_latent",
                     conv_layer_encoder="gatv2conv",
                     active_gp_thresh_ratio=0.01)
```

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:778-791]()

### Training Process

The training process involves these major steps:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant NicheCompass
    participant Trainer
    participant VGPGAE
    
    User->>NicheCompass: train()
    NicheCompass->>Trainer: initialize_trainer()
    Trainer->>Trainer: prepare_data()
    Trainer->>Trainer: initialize_dataloaders()
    
    loop For each epoch
        Trainer->>VGPGAE: forward_pass()
        VGPGAE->>VGPGAE: encode()
        VGPGAE->>VGPGAE: decode()
        VGPGAE-->>Trainer: outputs
        Trainer->>Trainer: compute_loss()
        Trainer->>Trainer: backward_pass()
        Trainer->>Trainer: update_parameters()
        
        alt Every n_epochs_all_gps epochs
            Trainer->>VGPGAE: get_active_gp_mask()
            VGPGAE-->>Trainer: active_gp_mask
            Trainer->>VGPGAE: update_active_gps()
        end
        
        Trainer->>Trainer: check_early_stopping()
    end
    
    Trainer-->>NicheCompass: trained_model
    NicheCompass-->>User: completed_training
```

Training involves optimizing multiple loss components:

| Loss Component | Description | Parameter |
|----------------|-------------|-----------|
| Edge Reconstruction | Loss for reconstructing spatial relationships | `lambda_edge_recon` |
| Gene Expression Reconstruction | Loss for reconstructing gene expression | `lambda_gene_expr_recon` |
| Chromatin Accessibility Reconstruction | Loss for reconstructing ATAC-seq data | `lambda_chrom_access_recon` |
| L1 Masked | Regularization for prior gene programs | `lambda_l1_masked` |
| L1 Addon | Regularization for de novo gene programs | `lambda_l1_addon` |

Example training code from the mouse brain multimodal tutorial:

```python
model.train(n_epochs=400,
            n_epochs_all_gps=25,
            lr=0.001,
            lambda_edge_recon=500000.,
            lambda_gene_expr_recon=300.,
            lambda_chrom_access_recon=300.,
            lambda_l1_masked=0.,
            lambda_l1_addon=30.,
            edge_batch_size=256,
            use_cuda_if_available=True,
            n_sampled_neighbors=4)
```

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:28-198]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:800-813]()

## Active Gene Programs

A key feature of the Core Model is its ability to identify "active" gene programs - those that significantly contribute to data reconstruction:

- During training, the model evaluates each gene program's contribution
- Gene programs with contributions below `active_gp_thresh_ratio` times the maximum contribution are considered inactive
- Only active gene programs are retained in the final latent representation

This mechanism ensures the latent space remains interpretable and focused on biologically meaningful dimensions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Model Training"] --> B["Evaluate GP Contributions"]
    B --> C["Calculate Maximum Contribution"]
    C --> D["Apply active_gp_thresh_ratio"]
    D --> E["Keep Only Active GPs"]
    E --> F["Interpretable Latent Space"]
```

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:134-152]()

## Supported Analysis Modalities

The Core Model supports several distinct analysis modalities:

### Single Sample Analysis

- Processes one spatial transcriptomics sample
- Creates an interpretable latent space of gene programs
- Enables cell-cell communication and niche identification

### Sample Integration

- Integrates multiple spatial samples
- Uses batch information to correct for batch effects
- Creates a unified latent space across samples

### Spatial Reference Mapping

- First trains on reference samples
- Maps query samples onto the reference latent space
- Maintains consistent gene program interpretation across samples

### Multimodal Analysis

- Integrates RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data
- Maps peaks to genes based on genomic proximity
- Creates a unified latent representation of both modalities

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb]()

## Technical Implementation

The Core Model is implemented in PyTorch with PyTorch Geometric extensions for graph operations. The model architecture is highly modular, allowing for customization of:

- Graph neural network types (GCN, GAT)
- Number of layers and hidden dimensions
- Loss function weightings
- Active gene program threshold
- Regularization parameters

The implementation follows a clean object-oriented design with three main classes:
- `NicheCompass`: User-facing API
- `VGPGAE`: Core model architecture
- `Trainer`: Training logic

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py]()
- [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py]()
- [environment.yaml:8-14]()

## Relation to Other NicheCompass Components

The Core Model is the central component of NicheCompass, interacting with other system components:

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    A --> C["Analysis Utilities"]
    
    B --> B1["Spatial Data Loading"]

    B --> B3["Multimodal Integration"]
    
    C --> C1["Cell-Cell Communication Analysis"]
    C --> C2["Visualization Tools"]
    C --> C3["Spatial Reference Mapping"]

```

# Gene Programs

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the Gene Programs component of NicheCompass, which provides a biologically interpretable foundation for analyzing spatial multi-omics data. Gene Programs are sets of functionally related genes derived from prior biological knowledge that NicheCompass uses to make its latent space interpretable and to understand cellular interactions in spatial context.

For information about how Gene Programs integrate with the core model architecture, see [Core Model](#2.1). For multimodal applications involving chromatin accessibility, see [Multimodal Integration](#2.3).

## What are Gene Programs?

Gene Programs (GPs) in NicheCompass represent collections of functionally related genes that participate in specific biological pathways or processes. Unlike general gene sets, NicheCompass's Gene Programs are designed to capture interactions between cells by distinguishing between:

1. **Source genes**: Genes expressed in transmitting/signaling cells (e.g., ligands, enzymes)
2. **Target genes**: Genes expressed in receiving cells (e.g., receptors, targets of transcription factors)

This source-target relationship makes Gene Programs particularly suitable for studying cell-cell communication in spatial data.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Gene Program Structure"
        A["Gene Program"] --> B["Source Genes"]
        A --> C["Target Genes"]
        B --> D["Transmitting Cell\nExpression"]
        C --> E["Receiving Cell\nExpression"]
        B -.-> |"Interaction"| C
    end
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:40-121]()

## Types of Gene Programs

NicheCompass supports several types of biologically informed Gene Programs, each capturing different aspects of cellular communication:

| Gene Program Type | Source Genes | Target Genes | Biological Focus |
|-------------------|--------------|--------------|------------------|
| OmniPath | Ligands | Receptors | Direct cell-cell communication via ligand-receptor pairs |
| NicheNet | Ligands | Receptors + Target genes | Extended pathway from ligand-receptor to downstream effects |
| MEBOCOST | Enzymes | Sensors | Metabolic interactions |
| CollecTRI | - | Transcription factors + Target genes | Transcriptional regulation networks |

These Gene Programs can be used individually or combined to provide a comprehensive framework for understanding different types of cellular interactions.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Gene Program Types in NicheCompass"
        GP["Gene Program Dictionary"] --> OP["OmniPath\nLigand-Receptor GPs"]
        GP --> NN["NicheNet\nLigand-Target GPs"]
        GP --> MB["MEBOCOST\nEnzyme-Sensor GPs"]
        GP --> CT["CollecTRI\nTF-Target GPs"]
        
        OP --> LR["Ligand-Receptor\nInteractions"]
        NN --> LT["Ligand-Receptor-Target\nPathways"]
        MB --> ES["Metabolic\nInteractions"]
        CT --> TT["Transcriptional\nRegulation"]
        
        LR & LT & ES & TT --> COMBINED["Combined GP Set"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:322-428](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:299-405]()

## Gene Program Creation

NicheCompass provides utility functions to extract Gene Programs from various databases. The extraction process typically involves:

1. Retrieving interaction data from a database
2. Converting gene names to a standardized format
3. Structuring the data into a Gene Program dictionary
4. Combining and filtering Gene Programs from different sources

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Gene Program Creation Process"
        A["External Databases"] --> B["extract_gp_dict_from_*\nFunctions"]
        B --> C["Individual GP Dictionaries"]
        C --> D["filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps"]
        D --> E["Combined GP Dictionary"]
        E --> F["add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata"]
        F --> G["GP Masks in AnnData"]
    end
```

The major utility functions for Gene Program creation include:

- `extract_gp_dict_from_omnipath_lr_interactions()`: Creates ligand-receptor GPs from OmniPath
- `extract_gp_dict_from_nichenet_lrt_interactions()`: Creates ligand-target GPs from NicheNet
- `extract_gp_dict_from_mebocost_ms_interactions()`: Creates enzyme-sensor GPs from MEBOCOST
- `extract_gp_dict_from_collectri_tf_network()`: Creates transcription factor GPs from CollecTRI
- `filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps_v2()`: Combines and filters GPs from multiple sources

Each Gene Program is structured as a dictionary entry with the following format:

```
"GP_Name": {
    "sources": ["GeneA", "GeneB", ...],  # Source genes (e.g., ligands)
    "targets": ["GeneC", "GeneD", ...],  # Target genes (e.g., receptors)
    "sources_categories": ["CategoryA", ...],  # Categories for source genes
    "targets_categories": ["CategoryB", ...]   # Categories for target genes
}
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:683-1193](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:299-405]()

## Adding Gene Programs to Data

Once created, Gene Programs need to be added to the AnnData object used by NicheCompass. This is done using the `add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata` function, which:

1. Converts Gene Programs into binary masks for sources and targets
2. Aligns these masks with genes present in the expression data
3. Filters Gene Programs based on minimum and maximum gene criteria
4. Adds the masks to the AnnData object as sparse matrices

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Adding Gene Programs to AnnData"
        A["GP Dictionary"] --> B["Create Binary Masks"]
        B --> C["Align with Genes in Data"]
        C --> D["Filter GPs by Gene Count"]
        D --> E["Add Masks to AnnData"]
        
        subgraph "AnnData Object"
            E --> F["adata.varm[gp_targets_mask_key]"]
            E --> G["adata.varm[gp_sources_mask_key]"]
            E --> H["adata.uns[gp_names_key]"]
        end
    end
```

Key parameters for adding Gene Programs:

- `min_genes_per_gp`: Minimum number of genes required in a GP
- `min_source_genes_per_gp`: Minimum number of source genes required
- `min_target_genes_per_gp`: Minimum number of target genes required
- `max_genes_per_gp`: Maximum number of genes allowed in a GP

These parameters help ensure that the Gene Programs included in the analysis have sufficient biological relevance and are well-represented in the dataset.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:18-168](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:467-484]()

## Gene Programs in the NicheCompass Model

Gene Programs form a core component of the NicheCompass model architecture. They provide a biologically interpretable structure to the latent space through the use of linear masked decoders.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Gene Programs in NicheCompass Model"
        INPUT["Input Data\n(Gene Expression)"] --> ENCODER["Graph Neural Network\nEncoder"]
        ENCODER --> LATENT["Latent Representation"]
        
        subgraph "Gene Program Interpretation"
            GP["Gene Program Masks"] --> MDECODERS["Masked Linear Decoders"]
            LATENT --> MDECODERS
        end
        
        MDECODERS --> OUTPUT["Reconstructed\nGene Expression"]
        
        LATENT --> ACTIVE["Active GP Selection"]
        ACTIVE --> INTLATENT["Interpretable\nLatent Space"]
    end
```

Key aspects of how Gene Programs are used in the model:

1. **Initialization**: Gene Programs are provided to the model as binary masks during initialization
2. **Active GP Selection**: During training, NicheCompass identifies which Gene Programs are most informative using an activation threshold ratio
3. **Latent Representation**: The latent space of the model can be interpreted in terms of Gene Program activities
4. **Gene Expression Reconstruction**: Masked linear decoders use Gene Programs to reconstruct gene expression patterns
5. **Cell-Cell Communication**: The source-target structure of Gene Programs allows inference of cell-cell communication

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:24-188](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:782-813]()

## Implementation Details

### Gene Program Masks

The Gene Program information is stored in the AnnData object as binary masks:

- `adata.varm[gp_targets_mask_key]`: Binary matrix (genes × gene programs) for target genes
- `adata.varm[gp_sources_mask_key]`: Binary matrix (genes × gene programs) for source genes
- `adata.uns[gp_names_key]`: List of Gene Program names

These masks define which genes belong to which Gene Programs, allowing the model to use this structured prior knowledge during training.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Gene Program Mask Structure"
        A["AnnData Object"] --> B["adata.varm[gp_targets_mask_key]"]
        A --> C["adata.varm[gp_sources_mask_key]"]
        A --> D["adata.uns[gp_names_key]"]
        
        subgraph "Binary Mask Matrix"
            B --> E["Genes (rows) × Gene Programs (columns)"]
            C --> E
        end
        
        E --> |"1 = Gene belongs to GP\n0 = Gene does not belong to GP"| F["Masked Linear Decoder"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:179-257]()

### Active Gene Programs

During model training, NicheCompass identifies which Gene Programs are most informative for explaining the data using an activation threshold:

```python
active_gp_thresh_ratio = 0.01  # Example threshold
```

Gene Programs with aggregated decoder weights below this threshold (relative to the maximum) are considered inactive and are dropped from the final latent representation. This helps focus the analysis on the most relevant biological pathways.

The active Gene Programs are stored in:
- `adata.uns[active_gp_names_key]`: List of active Gene Program names
- `adata.obsm[latent_key]`: Latent representation limited to active Gene Programs

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:134-147](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:133-159]()

## Using Gene Programs for Analysis

After training a NicheCompass model, the Gene Program-based latent space can be used for various analyses:

1. **Niche Identification**: Clustering cells based on their Gene Program activities
2. **Cell-Cell Communication**: Analyzing which cell types communicate through which Gene Programs
3. **Differential Gene Program Analysis**: Identifying Gene Programs that are differentially active between conditions or cell types
4. **Spatial Mapping**: Using Gene Program activities for spatial reference mapping across samples

These analyses leverage the biological interpretability of Gene Programs to provide meaningful insights into cell-cell interactions in spatial context.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Gene Program Analysis Workflow"
        A["Trained NicheCompass Model"] --> B["GP-Based Latent Space"]
        B --> C["Cell Clustering"]
        B --> D["Differential GP Analysis"]
        B --> E["Cell-Cell Communication\nNetwork Inference"]
        B --> F["Spatial Reference Mapping"]
        
        C & D & E & F --> G["Biological Interpretation"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:682-937](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:855-949]()

## Customization and Extension

Users can customize Gene Programs based on their specific research questions:

1. **Custom Gene Program Definition**: Create your own Gene Program dictionary with source and target genes
2. **Gene Program Filtering**: Adjust filtering parameters to focus on specific pathways
3. **De Novo Gene Programs**: NicheCompass can learn additional Gene Programs not defined in prior knowledge
4. **Multimodal Gene Programs**: For multimodal data, Gene Programs can be extended to include chromatin accessibility features

This flexibility allows NicheCompass to be adapted to various biological systems and research questions.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py:675-1264](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:674-714]()

- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb)
- [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py](src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py)

</details>



This page describes NicheCompass's multimodal integration system, which enables joint analysis of RNA-seq (gene expression) and ATAC-seq (chromatin accessibility) data. The integration maps genomic peaks to genes based on their chromosomal proximity, allowing the model to incorporate both data types in its variational gene program graph autoencoder. For information about the core model architecture, see [Core Model](#2.1), and for details about gene programs, see [Gene Programs](#2.2).

## System Overview

The multimodal integration workflow connects RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data through genomic annotation and mapping, creating specialized masks that link gene programs with their corresponding chromatin accessibility regions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["RNA-seq Data"] --> B["Gene Annotation"]
    C["ATAC-seq Data"] --> D["Peak Annotation"]
    B --> E["Gene-Peak Mapping"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["Multimodal Mask Creation"]
    F --> G["NicheCompass Model with\nRNA & ATAC Decoders"]
    G --> H["Integrated Analysis"]
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:673-686](), [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:17-105]()

## Key Components and Functions

### Gene Annotation System

The `get_gene_annotations()` function adds genomic positions to genes and peaks by linking with a GTF annotation file. This creates the foundation for mapping between the two modalities.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `adata` | AnnData RNA object for gene annotations |
| `adata_atac` | AnnData ATAC object to annotate |
| `gtf_file_path` | Path to GTF file with genomic positions |
| `drop_unannotated_genes` | Whether to remove genes without annotations |

### Gene-Peak Mapping

The `generate_multimodal_mapping_dict()` function builds a mapping between genes and peaks based on their genomic proximity, determining which peaks might influence which genes.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `adata` | AnnData RNA object with genes as features |
| `adata_atac` | AnnData ATAC object with peaks as features |
| `gene_region` | Region to consider: "combined", "promoter", or "gene_body" |
| `promoter_len` | Length of promoter regions in base pairs |
| `extend_range` | Maximum distance for mapping in base pairs |

### Multimodal Mask Creation

The `add_multimodal_mask_to_adata()` function creates masks linking gene programs to corresponding peaks, which the model uses to integrate the modalities.

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `adata` | AnnData RNA object with gene program masks |
| `adata_atac` | AnnData ATAC object for peak masks |
| `gene_peak_mapping_dict` | Dictionary mapping genes to peaks |
| `filter_peaks_based_on_genes` | Whether to keep only peaks mapped to genes |
| `gp_targets_mask_key` | Key for target gene program mask |
| `gp_sources_mask_key` | Key for source gene program mask |
| `ca_targets_mask_key` | Key for target chromatin accessibility mask |
| `ca_sources_mask_key` | Key for source chromatin accessibility mask |

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:107-193](), [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:196-382]()

## Integration Workflow

The following diagram illustrates the detailed multimodal integration process:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["RNA-seq Data (adata)"] --> B["get_gene_annotations()"]
    C["ATAC-seq Data (adata_atac)"] --> B
    B --> D["Annotated RNA Data\nwith Genomic Positions"]
    B --> E["Annotated ATAC Data\nwith Genomic Positions"]
    D --> F["generate_multimodal_mapping_dict()"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["Gene-Peak Mapping Dictionary"]
    G --> H["add_multimodal_mask_to_adata()"]
    D --> H
    E --> H
    H --> I["RNA Data with\nGene-Peak Mask"]
    H --> J["ATAC Data with\nChromatin Accessibility Masks"]
    I --> K["NicheCompass(adata, adata_atac, ...)"]
    J --> K
    K --> L["Trained Model with\nMultimodal Integration"]
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:595-714]()

## Integration with the NicheCompass Model

This diagram shows how multimodal data is processed within the NicheCompass model architecture:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: RNA Data (adata)"] --> B["Encoder"]
    AA["Input: ATAC Data (adata_atac)"] --> B
    B --> C["Latent Representation"]
    C --> D["RNA Decoder"]
    C --> E["Graph Decoder"]
    C --> F["ATAC Decoder"]
    D --> G["Reconstructed Gene Expression"]
    E --> H["Reconstructed Spatial Graph"]
    F --> I["Reconstructed Chromatin Accessibility"]
    
    subgraph "Multimodal Masks"
        J["Gene-Peak Mapping Mask"]
        K["GP Targets Chromatin Accessibility Mask"]
        L["GP Sources Chromatin Accessibility Mask"]
    end
    
    J --- D
    J --- F
    K --- F
    L --- F
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:774-800]()

## Step-by-Step Analysis Workflow

1. **Data Loading and Preprocessing**:
   - Load RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data as AnnData objects
   - Filter genes and peaks based on quality metrics and spatial variability

2. **Gene Program Creation**:
   - Create gene program masks from prior knowledge databases
   - Define target and source genes for each gene program

3. **Gene and Peak Annotation**:
   - Add chromosomal positions to genes and peaks using a GTF file

4. **Gene-Peak Mapping**:
   - Create mapping between genes and peaks based on genomic proximity
   - Consider promoters and gene bodies for mapping

5. **Multimodal Mask Creation**:
   - Create chromatin accessibility masks linking gene programs to peaks

6. **Model Training**:
   - Initialize NicheCompass with RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data
   - Train to integrate both modalities

7. **Integrated Analysis**:
   - Analyze the integrated data to gain biological insights

| Step | Description | Function/Method |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| 1 | Load data | `sc.read_h5ad()` |
| 2 | Create gene program masks | `add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata()` |
| 3 | Annotate genes and peaks | `get_gene_annotations()` |
| 4 | Create gene-peak mapping | `generate_multimodal_mapping_dict()` |
| 5 | Create multimodal masks | `add_multimodal_mask_to_adata()` |
| 6 | Initialize model | `NicheCompass(adata, adata_atac, ...)` |
| 7 | Train model | `model.train()` |

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:452-535](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:595-714](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:774-847]()

## Example: Mouse Brain Multimodal Analysis

The mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb tutorial demonstrates multimodal analysis of a postnatal day 22 coronal section from a spatial ATAC-RNA-seq mouse brain dataset (Zhang et al., 2023).

Dataset characteristics:
- 9,215 observations at spot resolution
- 22,914 probed genes
- 121,068 called peaks

The workflow includes:
1. Creating gene program masks from knowledge databases (OmniPath, NicheNet, MEBOCOST, CollecTRI)
2. Filtering spatially variable genes (3,000) and peaks (15,000)
3. Annotating genes and peaks with genomic positions
4. Creating a gene-peak mapping based on proximity
5. Adding multimodal masks to connect gene programs with corresponding peaks
6. Training a NicheCompass model with both modalities
7. Analyzing integrated results for spatial gene regulation insights

This example shows how NicheCompass integrates spatial RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data to understand relationships between chromatin accessibility and gene expression in spatial context.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:29-34](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:132-143](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:532-714]()

This document provides instructions for installing NicheCompass, a Python package for end-to-end analysis of spatial multi-omics data. For information about the overall architecture and system design, see [Architecture](#2).

## System Requirements

NicheCompass is compatible with Python 3.9 and does not currently support Apple silicon. The package requires several external dependencies, particularly PyTorch-related libraries which may need GPU support for optimal performance.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["System Requirements"] --> B["Python 3.9"]
    A --> C["CPU or CUDA-compatible GPU"]
    A --> D["Not supported on Apple Silicon"]
    A --> E["Virtual Environment Recommended"]
    
    E --> E1["Conda/Mambaforge"]
    E --> E2["Docker"]
    E --> E3["Python venv"]
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml:10-11](). [docs/installation.md:1-8]()

## Installation Methods

NicheCompass can be installed using pip after setting up the required external dependencies. We recommend using a virtual environment like conda or Docker rather than your system Python.

### Method 1: Using pip

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Install External Libraries"] --> B["Install PyTorch with CUDA"]
    A --> C["Install PyTorch Scatter/Sparse"]
    A --> D["Install bedtools"]
    B & C & D --> E["Install NicheCompass via pip"]
    E --> F["Install Optional Dependencies"]
```

Sources: [docs/installation.md:56-66]()

### Method 2: Using conda environment

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Create conda environment from file"] --> B["Activate environment"]
    B --> C["Install JAX with CUDA support"]
    C --> D["Ready to use NicheCompass"]
```

Sources: [docs/installation.md:39-43]()

## External Libraries Setup

Before installing NicheCompass, you'll need to set up several external libraries:

### PyTorch and PyTorch Extensions

Install PyTorch with appropriate CUDA support if available:

```bash
pip install torch==${TORCH}+${CUDA} --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/${CUDA}
pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-${TORCH}+${CUDA}.html
```

For example, for PyTorch 2.0.0 and CUDA 11.7:

```bash
pip install torch==2.0.0+cu117 --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu117
pip install pyg_lib torch_scatter torch_sparse -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-2.0.0+cu117.html
```

### bedtools

Install bedtools using conda:

```bash
conda install bedtools=2.30.0 -c bioconda
```

Sources: [docs/installation.md:12-37](), [.github/actions/setup/action.yaml:30-43]()

## NicheCompass Installation

### Basic Installation

After setting up the external libraries, install NicheCompass via pip:

```bash
pip install nichecompass
```

### Optional Dependencies

NicheCompass provides several optional dependency groups for different functionalities:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["nichecompass"] --> B["Core Package"]
    A --> C["Optional Dependencies"]
    
    C --> D["benchmarking"]
    C --> E["multimodal"]
    C --> F["tutorials"]
    C --> G["dev"]
    C --> H["docs"]
    C --> I["tests"]
    
    D --> D1["scib-metrics, pynndescent, etc."]
    E --> E1["scglue"]
    F --> F1["jupyter"]
    G --> G1["pre-commit, twine"]
    H --> H1["sphinx packages"]
    I --> I1["pytest, coverage"]
```

Install all optional dependencies:

```bash
pip install nichecompass[all]
```

Or install specific dependency groups:

```bash
pip install nichecompass[benchmarking,multimodal,tutorials]
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml:29-81](), [docs/installation.md:63-66]()

## Package Dependencies

The following table shows the core dependencies required by NicheCompass:

| Dependency | Version Requirement |
|------------|---------------------|
| mlflow | >=1.28.0 |
| pyreadr | >=0.4.6 |
| scanpy | >=1.9.3,<1.10.0 |
| torch-geometric | >=2.2.0 |
| omnipath | >=1.0.7 |
| decoupler | >=1.4.0 |
| numpy | <2 |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:29-37]()

## JAX GPU Support (Optional)

For enabling GPU support for JAX (used in benchmarking), run:

```bash
pip install jaxlib==0.4.7+cuda11.cudnn86 -f https://storage.googleapis.com/jax-releases/jax_cuda_releases.html
```

Replace with the appropriate CUDA version as needed.

Sources: [docs/installation.md:45-53](), [pyproject.toml:67-74]()

## Verification

After installation, you can verify that NicheCompass is properly installed by running:

```python
import nichecompass
print(nichecompass.__version__)
```

The output should match the version you installed.

Sources: [tests/test_basic.py:1-7]()


Sources: [docs/installation.md:1-73](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:42-49](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:39-43]()

The following diagram shows how the installation fits into the overall NicheCompass system architecture:

```mermaid
graph TD
```

This page provides an overview of the available tutorials for NicheCompass and suggests a learning path for new users. Each tutorial demonstrates key aspects of the NicheCompass framework for analyzing spatial multi-omics data, including spatial atlas building, niche identification, cell-cell communication inference, and spatial reference mapping.

## Available Tutorials

NicheCompass offers four main tutorial categories, each showcasing different capabilities of the framework:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NicheCompass Tutorials"] --> B["1. Single Sample Analysis"]
    A --> C["2. Multimodal Analysis"]
    A --> D["3. Sample Integration"]
    A --> E["4. Spatial Reference Mapping"]
    
    B --> B1["Mouse CNS 
    Single Sample"]
    C --> C1["Mouse Brain
    Multimodal"]
    D --> D1["Mouse CNS 
    Sample Integration"]
    E --> E1["Mouse CNS
    Spatial Reference Mapping"]
    
    subgraph "Learning Path"
        direction LR
        LP1["Start Here"] --> LP2["↓"] --> LP3["Advanced Use Cases"]
    end
    
    B -.-> LP1
    C -.-> LP2
    D -.-> LP2
    E -.-> LP3
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/single_sample_tutorials.md](), [docs/tutorials/multimodal_tutorials.md](), [docs/tutorials/sample_integration_tutorials.md](), [docs/tutorials/spatial_reference_mapping_tutorials.md]()

### 1. Single Sample Analysis

These tutorials demonstrate how to analyze a single spatial transcriptomics sample with NicheCompass. This is the recommended starting point for new users as it covers the core workflow and fundamental concepts.

**Available tutorial: Mouse CNS Single Sample**  
Analyzes a single sagittal brain section from the STARmap PLUS mouse central nervous system dataset.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb]()

### 2. Multimodal Analysis

These tutorials demonstrate how to analyze multimodal data (RNA-seq and ATAC-seq) with NicheCompass, showing how the framework can integrate multiple omics layers.

**Available tutorial: Mouse Brain Multimodal**  
Analyzes a single multimodal sample (postnatal day 22 coronal section) from the spatial ATAC-RNA-seq mouse brain dataset.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb]()

### 3. Sample Integration

These tutorials demonstrate how to integrate multiple spatial transcriptomics samples using NicheCompass, allowing for comparative analyses across samples.

**Available tutorial: Mouse CNS Sample Integration**  
Integrates three sagittal brain sections from the STARmap PLUS mouse central nervous system dataset.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb]()

### 4. Spatial Reference Mapping

These tutorials demonstrate how to perform spatial reference mapping across multiple samples, where a model is first trained on reference samples and then a query sample is mapped onto the reference.

**Available tutorial: Mouse CNS Spatial Reference Mapping**  
Uses two sagittal brain sections as reference samples and maps a third section as a query sample.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb]()

## Gene Program Creation Process

A central component in all tutorials is the creation of gene programs (GPs) from prior knowledge. This process follows these steps:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Extract GPs from Databases"] --> B["Filter and Combine GPs"]
    B --> C["Add GPs to AnnData"]
    
    subgraph "GP Sources"
        A1["OmniPath
        Ligand-Receptor"] --> A
        A2["NicheNet
        Ligand-Target"] --> A
        A3["MEBOCOST
        Enzyme-Sensor"] --> A
        A4["CollecTRI
        TF Network
        (optional)"] --> A
    end
    
    subgraph "GP Processing"
        B1["Filtering"] --> B2["Combining"] --> B3["Validation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "GP Integration"
        C1["Create Target Mask"] --> C3["Add to AnnData"]
        C2["Create Source Mask"] --> C3
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:300-485](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:324-668]()

## Model Training Process

Each tutorial demonstrates the model training process with NicheCompass:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Data Preparation"] --> B["Model Initialization"]
    B --> C["Model Training"]
    C --> D["Model Evaluation"]
    D --> E["Model Saving"]
    
    subgraph "Model Components Used"
        F1["NicheCompass Class"] --> F2["train() Method"]
        F2 --> F3["save() Method"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Parameters"
        G1["n_epochs"] 
        G2["lambda_edge_recon"]
        G3["lambda_gene_expr_recon"]
        G4["lambda_l1_addon"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:547-611](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:784-847]()

## Analysis Workflow

After training, each tutorial demonstrates how to analyze the results:

1. Load the trained model (or use the model from training)
2. Visualize the latent space representations
3. Identify niches or cell types
4. Analyze cell-cell communication

The specific analyses vary between tutorials based on the use case.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:620-900](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:855-1900]()

## Adapting Tutorials for Custom Data

While the tutorials use specific datasets, they can be adapted for custom data by:

1. Preparing your data in AnnData format
2. Adjusting parameters to match your dataset characteristics
3. Following the same workflow steps

You'll need to ensure your data contains:
- Spatial coordinates
- Gene expression counts
- (Optionally) Cell type annotations for evaluation
- (For multimodal analysis) Corresponding ATAC-seq data

## Suggested Learning Path

1. **Start with Single Sample Analysis**: Begin with the Mouse CNS Single Sample tutorial to understand the basic workflow and concepts.

2. **Explore Multimodal or Sample Integration**: Depending on your data, continue with either the Multimodal Analysis tutorial (if you have multi-omics data) or the Sample Integration tutorial (if you have multiple samples).

3. **Advanced: Spatial Reference Mapping**: Once familiar with the framework, explore the Spatial Reference Mapping tutorial for more advanced use cases.

Each tutorial builds on concepts from the previous ones, so following this order is recommended for new users.

## Computational Requirements

The tutorials are designed to run on systems with GPU acceleration, but can also run on CPU-only systems (with longer execution times). The specific requirements vary by tutorial:

| Tutorial | Memory Requirement | GPU Memory | Approx. Runtime (GPU) | Approx. Runtime (CPU) |
|----------|-------------------|------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Single Sample | 16GB+ | 8GB+ | 1-2 hours | 5-8 hours |
| Multimodal | 32GB+ | 16GB+ | 2-4 hours | 10-15 hours |
| Sample Integration | 32GB+ | 16GB+ | 3-5 hours | 12-24 hours |
| Spatial Reference Mapping | 32GB+ | 16GB+ | 4-6 hours | 15-30 hours |

For users with limited computational resources, each tutorial provides pre-trained models that can be used to run only the analysis sections.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:41-54](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:41-54]()

# Page: Single Sample Analysis

# Single Sample Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.readthedocs.yaml](.readthedocs.yaml)
- [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb)

</details>



This page describes the workflow for analyzing a single spatial omics sample using NicheCompass. Single sample analysis is the foundational use case for NicheCompass and provides a starting point for understanding cell niches and cell-cell communication within a single tissue section. For analyzing multiple samples, refer to [Sample Integration](#4.3) or [Spatial Reference Mapping](#4.4).

## Overview

NicheCompass enables comprehensive analysis of a single spatial omics sample through gene program (GP)-based modeling, providing insights into spatial relationships, cell-cell communication, and niche identification. The single sample analysis workflow consists of several key steps, from data preparation to visualizing results.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input Data<br>(Spatial Omics Sample)"] --> B["Data Preparation"]
    B --> C["GP Mask Creation"]
    C --> D["Spatial Neighborhood Graph"]
    D --> E["NicheCompass Model Training"]
    E --> F["Latent Space<br>Analysis"]
    F --> G1["Niche Identification"]
    F --> G2["Cell-Cell<br>Communication Analysis"]
    F --> G3["Spatial Feature<br>Visualization"]
    
    classDef mainStep fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class A,B,C,D,E,F,G1,G2,G3 mainStep;
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:26-32](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:608-619]()

## Data Requirements

For single sample analysis, NicheCompass requires:

1. A spatial omics dataset in AnnData format containing:
   - Expression count matrix
   - Spatial coordinates
   - Optionally cell type annotations

2. A gene program (GP) definition, either:
   - User-supplied gene program definitions
   - Automatically created from predefined databases

### Input Data Structure

The input data should conform to the following structure:

| Component | Description | Location in AnnData |
|-----------|-------------|---------------------|
| Expression counts | Raw or normalized gene expression values | `adata.layers["counts"]` |
| Spatial coordinates | 2D or 3D coordinates of each cell/spot | `adata.obsm["spatial"]` |
| Cell type annotations (optional) | Cell type labels | `adata.obs["cell_type"]` |

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:114-161](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:430-434]()

## Workflow Steps

### 1. Creating Prior Knowledge Gene Program Mask

Gene programs are key to the interpretability of NicheCompass. In single sample analysis, these programs capture biological pathways and cell-cell interactions.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Knowledge<br>Databases"] --> B["Gene Program<br>Extraction"]
    B --> C1["OmniPath<br>Ligand-Receptor GPs"]
    B --> C2["NicheNet<br>Ligand-Target GPs"]
    B --> C3["MEBOCOST<br>Enzyme-Sensor GPs"]
    
    C1 & C2 & C3 --> D["Filter & Combine"]
    D --> E["Gene Program<br>Mask"]
    E --> F["Add to AnnData"]
    
    classDef step fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class A,B,C1,C2,C3,D,E,F step;
```

NicheCompass offers utilities to create gene program masks from several sources:

1. **OmniPath**: Ligand-receptor interaction pairs
2. **NicheNet**: Ligand-receptor-target gene interactions  
3. **MEBOCOST**: Enzyme-sensor interactions for metabolic pathways
4. **CollecTRI**: Transcription factor networks (optional)

These GPs can be combined to create a comprehensive mask that captures different biological interactions.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:280-405]()

### 2. Spatial Neighborhood Graph Construction

NicheCompass leverages the spatial organization of cells/spots through a neighborhood graph:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Spatial<br>Coordinates"] --> B["Compute Neighbors<br>(sq.gr.spatial_neighbors)"]
    B --> C["Spatial<br>Adjacency Matrix"]
    C --> D["Symmetrize Matrix"]
    D --> E["Store in<br>adata.obsp['spatial_connectivities']"]
    
    classDef step fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class A,B,C,D,E step;
```

The spatial graph captures physical proximity relationships between cells or spots in the tissue section, which is essential for modeling spatial gene programs.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:412-453]()

### 3. Adding Gene Program Mask to Data

The function `add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata` adds the created gene program dictionary to the AnnData object as binary masks:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Gene Program<br>Dictionary"] --> B["Filter<br>Gene Programs"]
    B --> C["Create Binary<br>Mask Matrices"]
    C --> D["Store in<br>AnnData Object"]
    
    subgraph "Stored in AnnData"
        E["GP Target Mask<br>(Which genes are targets)"]
        F["GP Source Mask<br>(Which genes are sources)"]
        G["GP Names<br>(List of program names)"]
    end
    
    D --> E
    D --> F
    D --> G
```

The mask matrices indicate which genes belong to which gene programs as sources or targets, creating a structured representation of prior biological knowledge.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:459-485]()

### 4. Model Initialization and Training

The NicheCompass model uses a variational graph autoencoder architecture specialized for spatial gene program analysis:

```mermaid
graph TB
    A["Input:<br>AnnData with GP Masks"] --> B["NicheCompass"]
    B --> C["Encoder<br>(Graph Neural Network)"]
    C --> D["Latent Space<br>(Gene Programs)"]
    D --> E["Decoder"]
    E --> F1["Gene Expression<br>Reconstruction"]
    E --> F2["Graph<br>Reconstruction"]
    
    subgraph "Model Architecture"
        C
        D
        E
    end
    
    subgraph "Latent Space"
        G1["Prior Gene Programs"]
        G2["De Novo Gene Programs"]
    end
    
    D --- G1
    D --- G2
    
    classDef component fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class A,B,C,D,E,F1,F2,G1,G2 component;
```

The model training process involves:
1. Initializing the model with appropriate parameters
2. Training for a specified number of epochs
3. Computing a latent neighbor graph for downstream analysis
4. Saving the trained model for later analysis

Key parameters for training include:
- Number of epochs
- Learning rate
- Regularization weights
- Edge batch size for processing large graphs

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:529-611]()

### 5. Analysis of Results

After training, the NicheCompass model provides a latent representation of cells/spots organized by gene programs, enabling several types of analyses:

#### 5.1 Visualizing the Latent Space

The latent space can be visualized using UMAP or other dimensional reduction techniques to explore cell-type/niche organization:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Latent<br>Representation"] --> B["Compute Neighbors<br>sc.pp.neighbors"]
    B --> C["UMAP Projection<br>sc.tl.umap"]
    C --> D["Visualization<br>sc.pl.umap"]
    
    subgraph "Visualization Options"
        E["Cell Types"]
        F["Latent Clusters"]
        G["Gene Program Scores"]
    end
    
    D --> E
    D --> F
    D --> G
```

The UMAP visualization shows clusters of cells with similar gene program activities, often corresponding to specific cell types or functional states.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:586-597](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:683-693]()

#### 5.2 Niche Identification and Characterization

NicheCompass identifies cell niches based on the latent gene program space:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Latent<br>Representation"] --> B["Clustering<br>(Leiden Algorithm)"]
    B --> C["Niche<br>Identification"]
    C --> D["Enriched Gene<br>Program Analysis"]
    D --> E["Niche<br>Characterization"]
    
    classDef step fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class A,B,C,D,E step;
```

Niches are characterized by their enriched gene programs, providing insights into their functional properties and associated biological processes.

#### 5.3 Cell-Cell Communication Analysis

NicheCompass enables detailed analysis of cell-cell communication through its gene program structure:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Latent<br>Representation"] --> B["Compute Communication<br>Network"]
    B --> C["Network<br>Visualization"]
    C --> D1["Cell Type-Cell Type<br>Communication Strength"]
    C --> D2["Gene Program<br>Usage in Communication"]
    
    classDef step fill:#f9f9f9,stroke:#333,stroke-width:1px;
    class A,B,C,D1,D2 step;
```

The cell-cell communication analysis reveals which cell types are interacting and which gene programs mediate these interactions.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:683-693]()

## Best Practices for Single Sample Analysis

### Parameter Selection

When running single sample analysis, consider the following parameter choices:

| Parameter | Description | Recommended Values |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|
| `n_neighbors` | Number of spatial neighbors | 4-6 |
| `active_gp_thresh_ratio` | Threshold for active gene programs | 0.01-0.05 |
| `n_epochs` | Total training epochs | 300-500 |
| `n_epochs_all_gps` | Initial training with all GPs | 20-30 |
| `conv_layer_encoder` | Graph neural network layer type | "gcnconv" for standard analysis, "gatv2conv" for attention-based (requires more memory) |
| `edge_batch_size` | Batch size for edge decoding | Adjust based on available memory |

### Hardware Requirements

For a typical single sample analysis with 50,000-100,000 cells and 1,000-2,000 genes:
- RAM: 16+ GB (CPU processing)
- GPU Memory: 8+ GB (CUDA acceleration recommended)
- Storage: 2+ GB for model and results

Using GPU acceleration is highly recommended for datasets with more than 10,000 cells.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:124-161](), [docs/installation.md:19-25]()

## Example Workflow

A complete single sample analysis workflow typically follows these steps:

1. **Setup environment and import libraries**
   ```python
   import scanpy as sc
   import squidpy as sq
   from nichecompass.models import NicheCompass
   from nichecompass.utils import (add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata,
                                  extract_gp_dict_from_omnipath_lr_interactions,
                                  extract_gp_dict_from_nichenet_lrt_interactions,
                                  extract_gp_dict_from_mebocost_ms_interactions,
                                  filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps_v2)
   ```

2. **Create gene program dictionary from databases**
   ```python
   omnipath_gp_dict = extract_gp_dict_from_omnipath_lr_interactions(species="mouse")
   nichenet_gp_dict = extract_gp_dict_from_nichenet_lrt_interactions(species="mouse")
   mebocost_gp_dict = extract_gp_dict_from_mebocost_ms_interactions(species="mouse")
   combined_gp_dict = filter_and_combine_gp_dict_gps_v2([omnipath_gp_dict, nichenet_gp_dict, mebocost_gp_dict])
   ```

3. **Load data and compute spatial neighbors**
   ```python
   adata = sc.read_h5ad("sample.h5ad")
   sq.gr.spatial_neighbors(adata, coord_type="generic", spatial_key="spatial", n_neighs=4)
   ```

4. **Add gene program masks to data**
   ```python
   add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata(gp_dict=combined_gp_dict, adata=adata)
   ```

5. **Initialize and train model**
   ```python
   model = NicheCompass(adata)
   model.train(n_epochs=400)
   ```

6. **Analyze results**
   ```python
   sc.pp.neighbors(model.adata, use_rep="nichecompass_latent")
   sc.tl.umap(model.adata)
   sc.pl.umap(model.adata, color="cell_type")
   ```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:80-116](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:294-405](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:430-453](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:459-485](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:540-597]()

## Next Steps

After completing single sample analysis, you may want to explore:

1. [Multimodal Analysis](#4.2) - Integrating RNA-seq with ATAC-seq data
2. [Sample Integration](#4.3) - Integrating multiple spatial samples 
3. [Spatial Reference Mapping](#4.4) - Mapping new samples onto a spatial reference
