# Page: Multimodal Analysis

# Multimodal Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.readthedocs.yaml](.readthedocs.yaml)
- [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb)
- [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py](src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py)

</details>



This page documents NicheCompass's multimodal analysis capabilities, specifically the integration of RNA-seq (gene expression) and ATAC-seq (chromatin accessibility) data for spatial multi-omics analysis. Multimodal analysis in NicheCompass enables users to leverage complementary data types to gain deeper insights into cellular function and regulation within spatial context.

For information about integrating multiple samples of the same modality, see [Sample Integration](#4.3). For analyzing a single RNA-seq sample, refer to [Single Sample Analysis](#4.1).

## Overview of Multimodal Analysis

NicheCompass supports the integration of RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data through a specialized gene-peak mapping approach that aligns chromatin accessibility measurements with gene programs. This integration preserves the biological interpretability of the latent space while adding information about regulatory elements and their potential relationship to gene expression patterns.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Multimodal Analysis Framework"
        RNA["RNA-seq Data"] --> GM["Gene Programs Mask"]
        ATAC["ATAC-seq Data"] --> GA["Genomic Annotations"]
        
        RNA & ATAC --> GPA["Gene-Peak Mapping"]
        GA --> GPA
        
        GPA --> CAM["Chromatin Accessibility Mask"]
        
        GM & CAM --> NC["NicheCompass Model"]
        
        NC --> LS["Latent Space\nRepresentation"]
        LS --> RA["Reconstructed RNA Data"]
        LS --> RAT["Reconstructed ATAC Data"]
        LS --> RG["Reconstructed Graph"]
        
        LS --> CA["Downstream\nMultimodal Analysis"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:28-35](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:682-698]()

## Data Requirements and Preparation

For multimodal analysis, NicheCompass requires:

1. An RNA-seq `AnnData` object with gene expression measurements
2. An ATAC-seq `AnnData` object with chromatin accessibility measurements
3. Gene annotations with chromosomal positions
4. Peak annotations with chromosomal positions

Both datasets should share the same spatial coordinates to enable proper integration within the spatial context.

### Required Dependencies

Multimodal analysis requires additional dependencies beyond the core NicheCompass package:

```
pip install nichecompass[all]
```

Key additional dependencies include:
- `scglue` - for gene-peak mapping functionality
- `bedtools` - for genomic operations

Sources: [docs/installation.md:63-66]()

## Multimodal Integration Pipeline

The multimodal integration process involves several key steps:

1. Gene program creation for RNA data
2. Spatial graph construction
3. Gene and peak annotation with genomic positions
4. Gene-peak mapping based on genomic proximity
5. Creation of chromatin accessibility masks aligned with gene programs
6. Joint modeling of RNA and ATAC data

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Multimodal Integration Pipeline"
        direction LR
        A1["RNA-seq Data"] --> B1["Gene Program\nExtraction"]
        A2["ATAC-seq Data"] --> B2["Peak\nFiltering"]
        
        B1 --> C1["RNA Gene\nProgram Mask"]
        B2 --> C2["Annotate Peaks\nwith Positions"]
        
        D1["Genomic\nAnnotations"] --> C3["Annotate Genes\nwith Positions"]
        A1 --> C3
        
        C2 & C3 --> E["Gene-Peak\nMapping"]
        
        E --> F["Chromatin\nAccessibility Mask"]
        
        C1 & F --> G["NicheCompass\nModel"]
        
        G --> H["Multimodal\nLatent Representation"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:300-337](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:602-714](), [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:17-104]()

## Gene-Peak Mapping

A critical step in multimodal analysis is the mapping between genes and peaks, which enables NicheCompass to integrate chromatin accessibility data with gene expression.

### How Gene-Peak Mapping Works

The mapping process identifies which peaks may regulate which genes based on their genomic proximity:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Gene-Peak Mapping Process"
        A["Genes with Genomic\nPositions"] --> B["Define Gene Regions"]
        C["Peaks with Genomic\nPositions"] --> D["Identify Overlapping\nRegions"]
        
        B --> D
        
        D --> E["Gene-Peak\nMapping Dictionary"]
        
        subgraph "Gene Region Options"
            F1["Promoter Only"]
            F2["Gene Body"]
            F3["Combined"]
        end
        
        B --> F1
        B --> F2
        B --> F3
        
        E --> G["Filter Peaks"]
        G --> H["Filtered Peaks with\nGene Associations"]
        
        E --> I["Create Chromatin\nAccessibility Mask"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:107-193](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:694-714]()

### Mapping Parameters

The gene-peak mapping can be customized with several parameters:

| Parameter | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `gene_region` | Region to consider for mapping (promoter, gene_body, or combined) | "combined" |
| `promoter_len` | Length of promoter region (bp upstream of TSS) | 2000 |
| `extend_range` | Maximum extended range (bp) beyond overlap | 0 |

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:107-193]()

## Chromatin Accessibility Mask

After mapping genes to peaks, NicheCompass creates a chromatin accessibility mask that aligns with the gene program structure, enabling joint modeling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility.

### Mask Creation Process

The chromatin accessibility mask is created by mapping gene program gene sets to corresponding peak sets:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Chromatin Accessibility Mask Creation"
        A["Gene Program Mask\n(RNA)"] --> B["Map Genes to Peaks"]
        C["Gene-Peak\nMapping Dict"] --> B
        
        B --> D["Create Source Peak\nMask"]
        B --> E["Create Target Peak\nMask"]
        
        D & E --> F["Chromatin Accessibility\nMask (ATAC)"]
        
        F --> G["NicheCompass Model\nwith RNA and ATAC Decoders"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:196-382](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:699-714]()

## Model Configuration for Multimodal Analysis

When using NicheCompass for multimodal analysis, several additional parameters need to be configured:

1. Providing both RNA and ATAC AnnData objects to the model initialization
2. Adding loss weights for chromatin accessibility reconstruction
3. Adding a decoder for ATAC data

### Key Model Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `adata_atac` | ATAC-seq AnnData object |
| `lambda_chrom_access_recon` | Weight for chromatin accessibility reconstruction loss |
| `atac_recon_loss` | Type of loss function for ATAC reconstruction |

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:784-791]()

## Example Workflow

Here's a typical workflow for multimodal analysis with NicheCompass:

1. **Generate gene program mask for RNA data**
   - Extract gene programs from prior knowledge databases
   - Add mask to RNA AnnData object

2. **Annotate genes and peaks with genomic positions**
   - Use reference genome annotations
   - Map chromosome positions to genes and peaks

3. **Create gene-peak mapping**
   - Map genes to nearby peaks
   - Filter peaks based on gene associations

4. **Add chromatin accessibility mask**
   - Translate gene program mask to peak space
   - Add mask to ATAC AnnData object

5. **Initialize and train NicheCompass model**
   - Provide both RNA and ATAC AnnData objects
   - Configure appropriate loss weights

6. **Analyze results**
   - Examine latent space representation
   - Identify regulatory relationships

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:291-460](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:602-714](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:784-847]()

## Technical Details

### Key Functions for Multimodal Analysis

NicheCompass provides several utility functions for multimodal data preparation:

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `get_gene_annotations` | Adds genomic position annotations to genes |
| `generate_multimodal_mapping_dict` | Creates mapping between genes and peaks |
| `add_multimodal_mask_to_adata` | Adds chromatin accessibility masks to AnnData objects |

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:17-104](), [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:107-193](), [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:196-382]()

### Genomic Region Definitions

NicheCompass allows different gene region definitions for peak-gene associations:

1. **Promoter only**: Only considers promoter regions upstream of transcription start sites
2. **Gene body**: Only considers the actual gene body from start to end
3. **Combined**: Considers both the gene body and promoter region (default)

The promoter length is configurable, defaulting to 2000bp upstream of the transcription start site.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/multimodal_mapping.py:107-193]()

## Limitations and Considerations

When performing multimodal analysis with NicheCompass, consider the following:

1. Computational requirements increase significantly with multimodal data, especially for ATAC-seq with many peaks
2. Peak filtering is often necessary to reduce computational load
3. The quality of the gene-peak mapping depends on the accuracy of genomic annotations
4. Performance may vary depending on the spatial resolution of the data

Filtering strategies include:
- Keeping only spatially variable peaks
- Filtering based on minimum cell detection threshold
- Using only peaks that map to genes of interest

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:534-584]()

# Page: Sample Integration

# Sample Integration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

This document describes the Sample Integration functionality in NicheCompass, which enables the joint analysis of multiple spatial transcriptomics samples. Sample Integration allows users to learn a unified representation across samples that preserves both gene program information and spatial context. For information about integrating multimodal data (RNA + ATAC), see [Multimodal Integration](#2.3), and for mapping query samples to a pre-established spatial reference, see [Spatial Reference Mapping](#4.4).

## Overview

Sample Integration in NicheCompass integrates multiple spatial transcriptomics samples into a unified latent space where similar cell types and niches align across samples while preserving the integrity of cell-cell communication and spatial relationships. Unlike typical gene expression integration methods, NicheCompass specifically accounts for the spatial organization of cells in each sample.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph "Sample Integration Workflow"
        A["Multiple Spatial Samples"] --> B["Preprocessing"]
        B --> C["Spatial Graph Construction"]
        B --> D["Gene Program Mask Creation"]
        C --> E["Combined Graph\n(Disconnected Components)"]
        D --> F["GP Mask Application"]
        E --> G["NicheCompass Model"]
        F --> G
        G --> H["Integrated Latent Space"]
        H --> I["Joint Analysis\nacross Samples"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:133-171], [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:432-507]

## Key Components

The Sample Integration process involves several key components that work together to achieve effective integration while preserving spatial context:

### 1. Batch-aware Model Architecture

NicheCompass implements batch-aware decoders that allow the model to account for technical and biological differences between samples during integration.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Batch-aware NicheCompass Architecture"
        A["Input: Combined AnnData\nwith batch annotations"] --> B["Encoder"]
        B --> C["Latent Representation"]
        C --> D["Batch-aware Decoder"]
        D --> E["Reconstructed Data"]
        
        subgraph "Key Components"
            F["Categorical Embeddings\nfor Batch Information"]
            G["Batch-specific Gene Expression\nReconstruction"]
        end
        
        A --> F
        F --> D
        C --> G
        G --> D
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:617-634]

### 2. Spatial Graph Combination

A critical aspect of sample integration is maintaining the spatial relationships within each sample while preventing artificial connections between samples.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Sample 1"
        S1N1["Node 1"] --- S1N2["Node 2"]
        S1N2 --- S1N3["Node 3"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Sample 2"
        S2N1["Node 1"] --- S2N2["Node 2"]
        S2N2 --- S2N3["Node 3"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Combined Graph"
        CS1["Sample 1 Subgraph"] 
        CS2["Sample 2 Subgraph"]
        
        subgraph "No Edges Between Samples"
            CS1 -.- |"No connection"| CS2
        end
    end
    
    S1 --> CS1
    S2 --> CS2
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:474-507]

## Implementation Details

### Pre-processing and Setup

Before initializing the NicheCompass model for sample integration, you need to:

1. Load multiple samples into separate AnnData objects
2. Process each sample individually, computing spatial neighbor graphs
3. Combine the samples into a single AnnData object with appropriate batch annotations
4. Create disconnected spatial graphs that preserve within-sample spatial relationships

For sample integration specifically, the model requires:

- A batch identifier in `adata.obs`
- Categorical covariate configuration for batch-aware processing

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:432-507]

### Model Configuration

The NicheCompass model for sample integration requires specific parameters:

```python
model = NicheCompass(adata,
                     counts_key="counts",
                     adj_key="spatial_connectivities",
                     cat_covariates_embeds_injection=["gene_expr_decoder"],
                     cat_covariates_keys=["batch"],
                     cat_covariates_no_edges=[True],
                     cat_covariates_embeds_nums=[3],
                     # ... other standard parameters
                    )
```

The key batch-specific parameters are:
- `cat_covariates_keys`: List of column names in `adata.obs` that contain batch information
- `cat_covariates_embeds_injection`: Where to inject the batch information (typically in the gene expression decoder)
- `cat_covariates_embeds_nums`: Dimensions of the embedding for each categorical covariate
- `cat_covariates_no_edges`: Whether to avoid using the batch information for edge prediction

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:617-634]

### Disconnected Graph Construction

A key implementation detail in sample integration is the construction of the combined spatial graph:

```python
# Combine spatial neighborhood graphs as disconnected components
batch_connectivities = []
len_before_batch = 0
for i in range(len(adata_batch_list)):
    if i == 0: # first batch
        after_batch_connectivities_extension = sp.csr_matrix(
            (adata_batch_list[0].shape[0],
            (adata.shape[0] -
            adata_batch_list[0].shape[0])))
        batch_connectivities.append(sp.hstack(
            (adata_batch_list[0].obsp[adj_key],
            after_batch_connectivities_extension)))
    # ... handling middle and last batches
adata.obsp[adj_key] = sp.vstack(batch_connectivities)
```

This creates a block-diagonal adjacency matrix where connections exist only within samples, not between them.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:474-507]

## Workflow Example

The full workflow for integrating multiple spatial transcriptomics samples with NicheCompass involves:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Load Multiple Spatial Samples"] --> B["Generate Prior Knowledge\nGene Program Masks"]
    A --> C["Compute Spatial\nNeighbor Graphs per Sample"]
    B --> D["Add GP Masks to Data"]
    C --> E["Combine Graphs as\nDisconnected Components"]
    D --> F["Initialize NicheCompass\nwith Batch Parameters"]
    E --> F
    F --> G["Train Model"]
    G --> H["Extract & Analyze\nIntegrated Latent Space"]
    H --> I["Perform Cross-sample\nComparative Analyses"]
    
    style A fill:#f9f9f9
    style B fill:#f9f9f9
    style C fill:#f9f9f9
    style D fill:#f9f9f9
    style E fill:#f9f9f9
    style F fill:#f9f9f9
    style G fill:#f9f9f9
    style H fill:#f9f9f9
    style I fill:#f9f9f9
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:290-685]

## Use Cases and Analysis

After integrating samples with NicheCompass, you can perform various analyses:

1. **Cross-sample niche identification**: Find common niches/microenvironments across samples
2. **Differential gene program analysis**: Compare gene program activity between samples
3. **Cell-cell communication analysis**: Examine how intercellular signaling differs between samples
4. **Visualization of integrated space**: UMAP or spatial visualization of the integrated data

The integrated latent space allows for direct comparison of samples while accounting for their spatial context and biological variability.

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:691-736]

## Practical Considerations

When using Sample Integration in NicheCompass, consider the following:

| Consideration | Description |
|---------------|-------------|
| Memory usage | Large samples require significant memory, especially during graph combination |
| Batch differences | Substantial technical or biological differences between samples may affect integration quality |
| Spatial resolution | Consistent spatial resolution across samples is recommended |
| Gene overlap | Samples should have substantial overlap in measured genes |
| Batch parameter tuning | Adjust `cat_covariates_embeds_nums` based on the number and complexity of samples |

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:166-179]

## Comparison with Other Integration Methods

NicheCompass Sample Integration differs from other integration approaches:

| Method | Approach | Preserves Spatial Context? | Batch Correction |
|--------|----------|----------------------------|------------------|
| NicheCompass Integration | Graph-based integration with gene programs | Yes | Categorical embeddings in decoders |
| NicheCompass Reference Mapping | Train on reference, map query | Yes | Sequential training |
| Seurat Integration | PCA-based anchoring | No | Canonical correlation analysis |
| SCANVI | Variational autoencoder | No | Batch labels in encoder |

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb:617-634], [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:637-675]

## Summary

Sample Integration in NicheCompass provides a powerful approach for analyzing multiple spatial transcriptomics samples together. By constructing disconnected spatial graphs and using batch-aware decoders, the method preserves the spatial context of each sample while enabling joint analysis in a unified latent space. This approach is particularly valuable for comparative studies across conditions, time points, or individuals, where both gene expression differences and spatial organization are important considerations.

---

# Page: Spatial Reference Mapping

# Spatial Reference Mapping

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.readthedocs.yaml](.readthedocs.yaml)
- [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb)

</details>



Spatial Reference Mapping in NicheCompass provides a framework for integrating new spatial omics data with an existing reference atlas. Unlike regular sample integration where all samples are processed together, this approach first builds a reference model from established samples, then maps new query samples to this reference by fine-tuning the pretrained model. This enables cross-sample comparison, knowledge transfer, and annotation of new samples based on the reference.

For information about regular multi-sample analysis without using a reference, see [Sample Integration](#4.3).

## Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph "Phase 1: Reference Model Training"
        A["Reference Data<br>(Multiple Samples)"] --> B["Compute Spatial<br>Neighbor Graphs"]
        B --> C["Build Combined<br>Adjacency Matrix"]
        D["Gene Program<br>Prior Knowledge"] --> E["Add GP Masks<br>to Reference Data"]
        C --> F["Train NicheCompass<br>Reference Model"]
        E --> F
    end

    subgraph "Phase 2: Query Mapping"
        G["Query Data<br>(New Sample)"] --> H["Compute Spatial<br>Neighbor Graph"]
        I["Pretrained<br>Reference Model"] --> J["Combine Query and<br>Reference Data"]
        H --> J
        J --> K["Fine-tune Model<br>with Combined Data"]
        K --> L["Mapped Query in<br>Reference Space"]
    end

    F --> I
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:26-39](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:433-444](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:602-686](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:702-865]()

## Key Components

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Reference Components"
        A["Reference Samples"] --> B["Spatial Graphs"]
        C["Gene Program Mask"] --> D["Reference Model"]
        B --> D
    end

    subgraph "Query Components"
        E["Query Sample"] --> F["Spatial Graph"]
        F --> G["Query Mapping"]
        D --> G
    end

    subgraph "Technical Components"
        H["Combined Adjacency Matrix"] --> I["Disconnected Graph Components"]
        J["Categorical Covariates<br>cat_covariates_keys"] --> K["Batch Effect Handling"]
        L["Fine-tuning Parameters<br>lr, lambda_*"] --> M["Mapping Control"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:134-182](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:452-510](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:739-816]()

## Workflow and Implementation

### 1. Prepare Reference Data

The first step involves selecting and processing reference samples:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A1["Reference Sample 1"] --> B1["Spatial Graph 1"]
    A2["Reference Sample 2"] --> B2["Spatial Graph 2"]
    B1 --> C["Combined Reference<br>Adjacency Matrix<br>(Disconnected Components)"]
    B2 --> C
    D["GP Mask<br>OmniPath/NicheNet/MEBOCOST"] --> E["Masked Reference Data"]
    C --> E
    E --> F["NicheCompass Model<br>Training"]
    F --> G["Saved Reference Model<br>and Embeddings"]
```

Key aspects of reference preparation:
- Multiple samples can be used as reference
- Each sample's spatial neighbor graph is computed separately
- Graphs are combined as disconnected components
- Gene program (GP) masks from prior knowledge make the latent space interpretable

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:452-510](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:527-543](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:619-687]()

### 2. Query Data Preparation and Mapping

After establishing a reference model, new query samples can be mapped:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Query Sample"] --> B["Query Spatial Graph"]
    C["Reference Data<br>with Embeddings"] --> D["Combined Data<br>(Reference + Query)"]
    B --> D
    E["Pretrained<br>Reference Model"] --> F["Fine-tuning<br>Process"]
    D --> F
    F --> G["Integrated Latent<br>Representation"]
    G --> H1["Joint Visualization"]
    G --> H2["Knowledge Transfer"]
    G --> H3["Cross-sample Analysis"]
```

Important considerations for query mapping:
- The query sample gets its own spatial graph
- Query and reference samples remain disconnected in the spatial adjacency matrix
- Fine-tuning preserves reference structure while incorporating query data
- Batch-specific parameters handle differences between reference and query

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:719-816](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:841-905](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:927-943]()

### 3. Technical Implementation

The spatial reference mapping framework uses several specific technical approaches:

#### Handling Batch Effects

Batch-specific parameters are essential for integrating reference and query data:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Handling Sample-Specific Effects"
        A["cat_covariates_keys=['batch']"] --> B["Sample Identity Tracking"]
        C["cat_covariates_embeds_injection=['gene_expr_decoder']"] --> D["Decoder-Specific<br>Batch Correction"]
        E["cat_covariates_embeds_nums=[3]"] --> F["Embedding Dimension<br>for Batch"]
        G["cat_covariates_no_edges=[True]"] --> H["No Edges Between<br>Different Batches"]
    end
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:143-159](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:624-635]()

#### Combined Adjacency Matrix Construction

The structure of the combined adjacency matrix is critical for proper reference mapping:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Reference Sample 1<br>Adjacency Matrix"] --> C["Block Diagonal<br>Structure"]
    B["Reference Sample 2<br>Adjacency Matrix"] --> C
    D["Query Sample<br>Adjacency Matrix"] --> E["Combined Matrix<br>with Zero Off-Diagonal<br>Blocks"]
    C --> E
    
    subgraph "Combined Adjacency Matrix"
        F["Ref1 <-> Ref1"] --- G["0"]
        G --- H["0"]
        I["0"] --- J["Ref2 <-> Ref2"]
        J --- K["0"]
        L["0"] --- M["0"]
        M --- N["Query <-> Query"]
    end
```

This structure ensures:
- Each sample's spatial relationships are preserved
- No artificial connections between different samples
- Disconnected components in the graph representation

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:475-508](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:788-815]()

## Example Usage

Below is a simplified workflow for spatial reference mapping with NicheCompass:

1. **Process Reference Samples**:
   ```python
   # Load reference samples
   adata_reference = process_reference_samples(reference_samples)
   
   # Add GP masks
   add_gps_from_gp_dict_to_adata(
       gp_dict=combined_gp_dict,
       adata=adata_reference,
       gp_targets_mask_key="nichecompass_gp_targets",
       # other parameters...
   )
   
   # Initialize and train reference model
   model = NicheCompass(
       adata_reference,
       cat_covariates_keys=["batch"],
       cat_covariates_embeds_injection=["gene_expr_decoder"],
       # other parameters...
   )
   
   model.train(n_epochs=400, lr=0.001, lambda_edge_recon=500000.)
   
   # Save reference model
   model.save(dir_path="reference_model")
   ```

2. **Map Query Samples**:
   ```python
   # Load query sample and pretrained reference model
   adata_query = process_query_sample(query_sample)
   model = NicheCompass.load(dir_path="reference_model")
   
   # Combine reference and query data
   adata_combined = combine_reference_and_query(
       adata_reference, adata_query
   )
   
   # Map query to reference by fine-tuning
   model.fine_tune(
       adata_combined,
       n_epochs=100,
       lr=0.0001,
       # other parameters...
   )
   
   # Analyze integrated data
   sc.pp.neighbors(model.adata, use_rep="nichecompass_latent")
   sc.tl.umap(model.adata)
   ```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:619-686](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:841-942]()

## Important Parameters

The following parameters are particularly important for spatial reference mapping:

| Parameter | Description | Typical Value |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| `cat_covariates_keys` | List of categorical variables identifying different samples | `["batch"]` |
| `cat_covariates_embeds_injection` | Where to inject batch-specific embeddings | `["gene_expr_decoder"]` |
| `cat_covariates_no_edges` | Whether to prevent edges between different batches | `[True]` |
| `n_epochs` (reference) | Number of epochs for reference model training | 400 |
| `n_epochs` (fine-tuning) | Number of epochs for query mapping | 100-200 |
| `lr` (fine-tuning) | Learning rate for fine-tuning (typically lower than reference training) | 0.0001-0.0005 |
| `lambda_edge_recon` | Weight for edge reconstruction loss | 500000.0 |
| `lambda_gene_expr_recon` | Weight for gene expression reconstruction loss | 300.0 |

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:142-182](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:646-655](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:904-909]()

## Advanced Analysis

After mapping query samples to the reference space, several analyses become possible:

1. **Cross-sample cell type identification**: Use reference annotations to identify cell types in the query sample
2. **Comparative gene program analysis**: Compare gene program activity between reference and query
3. **Niche identification**: Identify conserved and sample-specific cell niches
4. **Spatial pattern comparison**: Compare spatial organization between samples
5. **Cell-cell communication analysis**: Analyze and compare cell-cell interactions across samples

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:927-1196](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:1330-1369]()

## Use Cases

Spatial reference mapping is particularly valuable in these scenarios:

1. **Atlas Building**: Incrementally build spatial atlases by mapping new samples to established references
2. **Disease Studies**: Map disease samples to healthy reference to identify pathological changes
3. **Developmental Studies**: Map different developmental stages to a common reference
4. **Cross-technique Integration**: Map data from different spatial technologies to a common reference space
5. **Cross-species Comparison**: With appropriate gene homology mapping, compare spatial organization across species

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb:26-39]()

The Analysis Utilities module in NicheCompass provides essential tools for downstream analysis of the trained model results. These utilities enable researchers to extract biological insights from spatial multi-omics data through cell-cell communication analysis, visualization of gene programs, and benchmarking metrics.

## Overview

The Analysis Utilities in NicheCompass serve as the post-training analytical layer, helping users interpret the biological meaning of the latent representations and gene programs learned by the core model. They focus on three main areas:

1. Cell-Cell Communication Analysis - Tools to infer and quantify communication patterns between cell types
2. Visualization Tools - Functions to create informative plots of gene programs and cell-cell interactions
3. Benchmarking Tools - Metrics to evaluate model performance and spatial preservation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Trained NicheCompass Model"] --> B["Latent Representation"]
    B --> C["Analysis Utilities"]
    
    subgraph "Analysis Utilities"
        C1["Cell-Cell Communication Analysis"]
        C2["Visualization Tools"]
        C3["Benchmarking Tools"]
    end
    
    C --> C1
    C --> C2
    C --> C3
    
    C1 --> D1["Communication Networks"]
    C1 --> D2["Cell Type Aggregation"]
    
    C2 --> E1["Gene Program Visualization"]
    C2 --> E2["Chord Plot Creation"]
    C2 --> E3["Enrichment Plots"]
    
    C3 --> F1["CLISIS"]
    C3 --> F2["CAS (Cell type Adjacency Score)"]
    C3 --> F3["GCS (Graph Connectivity Score)"]
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/__init__.py](), [src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py:1-37]()

## Cell-Cell Communication Analysis

NicheCompass provides tools to analyze and visualize cell-cell communication patterns inferred from the learned gene programs and spatial relationships.

### Matrix Aggregation Functions

The `aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type` function aggregates matrices stored in `adata.obsp` (such as reconstructed adjacency matrices or aggregation weights) by cell type. This is a fundamental operation for cell-cell communication analysis:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["adata.obsp[obsp_key]"] --> B["aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type()"]
    B --> C["Cell Type Aggregated Matrix"]
    B --> D["Cell Type x Cell Type Matrix"]
    
    subgraph "Input Parameters"
        P1["obsp_key"]
        P2["cell_type_key"]
        P3["group_key (optional)"]
        P4["agg_rows (boolean)"]
    end
    
    P1 --> B
    P2 --> B
    P3 --> B
    P4 --> B
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:23-102]()

### Communication Network Visualization

Communication networks can be visualized using chord plots to illustrate interactions between different cell types:

1. `create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df` - Creates chord diagrams showing connections between cell types
2. `compute_communication_gp_network` - Computes communication networks based on gene programs
3. `visualize_communication_gp_network` - Visualizes the computed communication networks

The chord plots highlight the strength of interactions between different cell types, making it easy to identify major communication axes in the tissue.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:105-210](), [src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py:1-37]()

## Visualization Tools

NicheCompass offers several visualization utilities to help interpret the model results and discover biological patterns.

### Gene Program Visualization

The `generate_enriched_gp_info_plots` function creates comprehensive visualization of enriched gene programs:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"] --> B["Enriched GP Category Plot"]
    A --> C["GP Activity Score Plot"]
    A --> D["Top Source Gene Plots"]
    A --> E["Top Target Gene Plots"]
    A --> F["Top Source Peak Plots (if available)"]
    A --> G["Top Target Peak Plots (if available)"]
    
    subgraph "Key Parameters"
        P1["model: NicheCompass"]
        P2["sample_key: str"]
        P3["differential_gp_test_results_key: str"]
        P4["cat_key: str"]
        P5["cat_palette: dict"]
        P6["feature_spaces: list"]
    end
    
    P1 --> A
    P2 --> A
    P3 --> A
    P4 --> A
    P5 --> A
    P6 --> A
```

This function works by:
1. Computing gene and peak importances for selected gene programs
2. Creating spatial or UMAP plots showing the gene program activities
3. Displaying the top genes and peaks contributing to each gene program

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:212-404]()

### Information Plots

The helper function `plot_enriched_gp_info_plots_` handles the actual plotting mechanics of gene program information:

1. Creates a combined multi-panel figure with enriched category visualization
2. Displays gene program scores in the selected feature space
3. Shows expression/accessibility of top genes/peaks in the selected feature space

These plots help users understand which genes and peaks are most important for each gene program and how they are distributed in space.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:406-591]()

## Benchmarking Tools

NicheCompass includes several metrics to evaluate model performance, particularly focusing on the preservation of spatial relationships in the latent space.

### CLISIS (Cell Type Local Inverse Simpson's Index Similarity)

CLISIS measures how accurately the latent nearest neighbor graph preserves local neighborhood cell type heterogeneity from the spatial nearest neighbor graph:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Spatial KNN Graph"] --> C["Spatial Cell CLISI Scores"]
    B["Latent KNN Graph"] --> D["Latent Cell CLISI Scores"]
    
    C --> E["RCLISI = Latent CLISI / Spatial CLISI"]
    D --> E
    
    E --> F["Log Transformation"]
    F --> G["Normalization"]
    G --> H["CLISIS = 1 - median(|Normalized Log RCLISI|)"]
    
    subgraph "compute_clisis() Function"
        C
        D
        E
        F
        G
        H
    end
```

CLISIS ranges from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating better preservation of local neighborhood cell type heterogeneity in the latent representation.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py:1-203]()

### Additional Benchmarking Metrics

NicheCompass also provides other benchmarking metrics:

1. Cell type Adjacency Score (CAS) - Measures preservation of cell type adjacency patterns
2. Graph Connectivity Score (GCS) - Evaluates how well graph connectivity is preserved
3. Neighborhood Area Similarity Weighted (NASW) - Quantifies preservation of neighborhood areas
4. Multi-Label Adjusted Mutual Information (MLAMI) - Measures agreement between cluster assignments

These metrics can be computed using functions from the `benchmarking` module.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py:8-21]()

## Integration with NicheCompass Model

The analysis utilities are designed to work seamlessly with trained NicheCompass models. The `NicheCompass` class in `models/nichecompass.py` contains methods that utilize these utilities for analyzing model results.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["NicheCompass Model"] --> B["train()"]
    B --> C["Trained Model"]
    
    C --> D["Latent Representation"]
    C --> E["Reconstructed Gene Expression"]
    C --> F["Reconstructed Graph"]
    
    D --> G["Analysis Utilities"]
    E --> G
    F --> G
    
    G --> H1["aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type()"]
    G --> H2["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"]
    G --> H3["create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()"]
    G --> H4["compute_communication_gp_network()"]
    G --> H5["compute_clisis()"]
```

The analysis utilities can be used directly on the AnnData object containing the model results or through higher-level interfaces provided by the model itself.

Sources: [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py:24-589](), [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py:28-453]()

## Usage Example

Below is a typical workflow for using NicheCompass analysis utilities:

1. Train a NicheCompass model
2. Compute cell-cell communication networks
3. Create visualization of enriched gene programs
4. Evaluate model performance using benchmarking metrics

```python
# 1. Train model
model = NicheCompass(adata)
trainer = Trainer(adata, model)
trainer.train(n_epochs=100)

# 2. Analyze cell-cell communication
cell_type_agg_df = aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type(
    adata=adata,
    obsp_key="nichecompass_agg_weights",
    cell_type_key="cell_type",
    agg_rows=True
)

# 3. Visualize enriched gene programs
generate_enriched_gp_info_plots(
    plot_label="Tumor_Microenvironment",
    model=model,
    sample_key="sample",
    differential_gp_test_results_key="diff_gp_results",
    cat_key="cell_type",
    cat_palette=cell_type_colors,
    feature_spaces=["latent"]
)

# 4. Compute benchmarking metrics
clisis_score = compute_clisis(
    adata=adata,
    cell_type_key="cell_type",
    latent_key="nichecompass_latent"
)
```

## Summary

The Analysis Utilities in NicheCompass provide comprehensive tools for extracting biological insights from spatial multi-omics data after model training. These utilities enable researchers to:

1. Identify and quantify cell-cell communication networks
2. Visualize gene programs and their spatial distributions
3. Benchmark model performance in preserving spatial relationships

For cell-cell communication analysis specifically, see [Cell-Cell Communication Analysis](#5.1).  
For more on visualization capabilities, see [Visualization Tools](#5.2).  
For benchmarking details, see [Benchmarking Tools](#5.3).

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py:1-37](), [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py:8-21](), [pyproject.toml:29-81]()

# Page: Cell-Cell Communication Analysis

# Cell-Cell Communication Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.readthedocs.yaml](.readthedocs.yaml)
- [docs/index.md](docs/index.md)
- [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md)
- [docs/release_notes/index.md](docs/release_notes/index.md)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb)
- [docs/user_guide/index.md](docs/user_guide/index.md)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
- [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py](src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py)

</details>



This document explains the Cell-Cell Communication Analysis system in NicheCompass, which allows users to infer and analyze communication networks between cells in spatial multi-omics data. The system leverages gene programs extracted from various biological databases to identify potential cell-cell interactions and provides utilities for visualizing and interpreting these communication patterns.

## Purpose and Scope

The Cell-Cell Communication Analysis component of NicheCompass enables researchers to:

1. Identify and quantify cell-cell interactions based on gene program activities
2. Construct communication networks between cell types
3. Visualize communication patterns using chord plots and other informative visualizations
4. Analyze enriched gene programs involved in cell-cell communication

This document focuses specifically on the communication analysis tools. For information about gene program creation, see [Gene Programs](#2.2). For information about the core model architecture, see [Core Model](#2.1).

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:104-114]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:98-103]()

## Communication Analysis Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Trained NicheCompass Model"] --> B["Latent GP Representation"]
    B --> C["Cell-Cell Communication Analysis"]
    
    C --> D["Communication Network Computation"]
    D --> E["Network Visualization"]
    
    subgraph "Input Data Sources"
        GP1["OmniPath Ligand-Receptor"]
        GP2["NicheNet Ligand-Target"]
        GP3["MEBOCOST Enzyme-Sensor"]
        GP4["CollecTRI TF Network"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Process"
        D1["compute_communication_gp_network()"]
        D2["Identify Significant Connections"]
        D3["Create Cell Type Aggregated Matrix"]
        D1 --> D2 --> D3
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization Options"
        E1["visualize_communication_gp_network()"]
        E2["create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()"]
        E3["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"]
    end
    
    GP1 & GP2 & GP3 & GP4 --> A
    D --> D1
    E --> E1 & E2 & E3
```

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:104-114]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:98-103]()
- [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:23-102]()

## Core Components

### Communication Network Computation

The core of cell-cell communication analysis in NicheCompass is based on analyzing gene programs (GPs) that represent known biological interaction pathways. Communication networks are computed based on the activity of these gene programs in spatial context.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["NicheCompass Model"] --> B["Latent GP Activities"]
    
    subgraph "Key Computation Functions"
        C1["compute_communication_gp_network()"]
    end
    
    B --> C1
    C1 --> D["Communication Network"]
    
    D --> E1["Cell Type Interactions"]
    D --> E2["GP-based Communication Patterns"]
    D --> E3["Spatial Communication Context"]
    
    style C1 font-weight:bold
```

The `compute_communication_gp_network()` function analyzes gene program activities to identify significant cell-cell communications. It processes:

1. Source GPs (e.g., ligands in ligand-receptor interactions)
2. Target GPs (e.g., receptors in ligand-receptor interactions)
3. Cell type annotations
4. Spatial neighborhood information

The result is a directed network where nodes represent cell types and edges represent communication strength between them, weighted by the activities of relevant gene programs.

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:104-114]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:98-103]()

### Aggregation of Communication Data

Communication data is often aggregated at the cell type level to identify patterns of interaction between different cell populations.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Raw Communication Matrix 
    (Cell-to-Cell Level)"] --> B["aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type()"]
    
    B --> C["Cell Type Aggregated Matrix"]
    
    C --> D["Cell Type Communication Analysis"]
    C --> E["Chord Plot Visualization"]
    C --> F["Enriched GP Analysis"]
    
    style B font-weight:bold
```

The `aggregate_obsp_matrix_per_cell_type()` function (found in [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:23-102]()) aggregates adjacency matrices stored in `adata.obsp` at the cell type level. It can process:

- The node label aggregator weights
- Reconstructed adjacency matrices
- Other matrices in the observation-by-observation space

This aggregation allows analysis of communication patterns between cell types rather than individual cells, making it easier to interpret biological significance.

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:23-102]()

## Visualization Methods

NicheCompass provides several visualization methods to interpret cell-cell communication results:

### Communication Network Visualization

The `visualize_communication_gp_network()` function creates network visualizations showing communication between cell types. These visualizations can display:

- Cell types as nodes
- Communication strength as edge weights
- Gene programs involved in communication

### Cell Type Chord Plots

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Aggregated Communication Matrix"] --> B["create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()"]
    
    B --> C["Cell Type Chord Diagram"]
    
    C --> D["Visualization of Cell Type Interactions"]
    
    subgraph "Parameters"
        P1["link_threshold"]
        P2["cell_type_key"]
        P3["group_key"]
    end
    
    P1 & P2 & P3 --> B
    
    style B font-weight:bold
```

The `create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()` function creates chord diagrams that visualize communication between cell types. These circular plots show:

- Cell types around the circumference
- Connecting chords representing communication strength
- Directionality of communication (source to target)

The function applies a threshold to display only significant connections based on the link strength ratio compared to the maximum.

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:105-210]()

### Enriched Gene Program Information Plots

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Trained NicheCompass Model"] --> B["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"]
    
    subgraph "Input Parameters"
        C1["model: NicheCompass"]
        C2["differential_gp_test_results_key"]
        C3["cat_key: Category to Color"]
        C4["feature_spaces: e.g. 'latent'"]
    end
    
    C1 & C2 & C3 & C4 --> B
    
    B --> D["Enriched GP Info Plots"]
    
    D --> E1["Enriched Category Visualization"]
    D --> E2["GP Activity Scores"]
    D --> E3["Top Genes Expression"]
    D --> E4["(Optional) Top Peaks Accessibility"]
    
    style B font-weight:bold
```

The `generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()` function visualizes gene programs involved in cell-cell communication. For each gene program, it displays:

1. The enriched cell type category
2. Gene program activity scores
3. Expression of top genes associated with the gene program
4. (If applicable) Accessibility of top peaks associated with the gene program

These visualizations help interpret which gene programs are active in which cell types and their potential role in cell-cell communication.

Sources:
- [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:212-632]()

## Usage Example

Below is a typical workflow for performing cell-cell communication analysis with NicheCompass:

1. Train a NicheCompass model with gene programs that represent biological interaction pathways (e.g., ligand-receptor, enzyme-sensor)
2. Compute the communication network between cell types
3. Visualize the network using chord plots or other network visualizations
4. Analyze enriched gene programs to interpret biological significance

Example code from the tutorials:

```python
# Compute communication network between cell types
communication_df = compute_communication_gp_network(
    model=model,
    cell_type_key=cell_type_key,
    sample=samples[0]
)

# Visualize the communication network
visualize_communication_gp_network(
    model=model,
    communication_df=communication_df,
    plot_label="Communication Network",
    save_fig=True,
    figure_folder_path=figure_folder_path
)

# Generate enriched gene program info plots
generate_enriched_gp_info_plots(
    plot_label="Enriched_GPs",
    model=model,
    sample_key=sample_key,
    differential_gp_test_results_key=differential_gp_test_results_key,
    cat_key=cell_type_key,
    cat_palette=cell_type_colors,
    n_top_genes_per_gp=3,
    feature_spaces=["latent"],
    save_figs=True,
    figure_folder_path=figure_folder_path
)
```

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:104-114]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:98-103]()

## Data Requirements

To perform cell-cell communication analysis with NicheCompass, you need:

| Requirement | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| Trained NicheCompass model | A model trained on spatial data with gene programs |
| Cell type annotations | Labels indicating cell type for each observation |
| Gene program masks | Binary masks indicating which genes belong to which programs |
| Spatial information | Coordinates and neighborhood graph of cells/spots |

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:104-114]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:98-103]()

## Integration with Biological Knowledge

NicheCompass leverages multiple sources of biological knowledge for cell-cell communication analysis:

| Database | Purpose | Type of Interactions |
|----------|---------|----------------------|
| OmniPath | Ligand-Receptor interactions | Cell-to-cell signaling |
| NicheNet | Ligand-Target interactions | Signaling effects on target genes |
| MEBOCOST | Enzyme-Sensor interactions | Metabolic communication |
| CollecTRI | Transcription Factor networks | Gene regulatory networks |

This integration helps connect the computational analysis to biological mechanisms of cell-cell communication.

Sources:
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:324-342]()
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:322-340]()

## Summary

The Cell-Cell Communication Analysis system in NicheCompass provides a comprehensive toolset for inferring, analyzing, and visualizing communication patterns between cells in spatial multi-omics data. By leveraging gene programs from various biological databases, it connects computational analysis to biological mechanisms of cell-cell communication, making it a valuable tool for understanding cellular interactions in complex tissues.

# Page: Visualization Tools

# Visualization Tools

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [docs/index.md](docs/index.md)

- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb)

NicheCompass provides a comprehensive suite of visualization tools designed to help researchers interpret the results of spatial multi-omics analyses. These tools enable the visualization of data in both physical and latent spaces, exploration of gene programs, and analysis of cell-cell communication patterns. This page describes the primary visualization tools available in NicheCompass and how to use them effectively.

For information about cell-cell communication analysis methods, see [Cell-Cell Communication Analysis](#5.1).

## Visualization Framework Overview

NicheCompass visualization tools leverage several Python libraries, including Matplotlib, Scanpy, Squidpy, Seaborn, and NetworkX. The visualization utilities are primarily accessed through functions in the `nichecompass.utils` module.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["NicheCompass Visualization Framework"] --> B["Spatial Visualization"]
    A --> C["Latent Space Visualization"]
    A --> D["Gene Program Visualization"]
    A --> E["Cell-Cell Communication Visualization"]
    
    B --> B1["Spatial Cell Type Plots"]
    B --> B2["Spatial Gene Expression Plots"]
    B --> B3["Spatial Gene Program Activity Plots"]
    
    C --> C1["UMAP Embeddings"]
    C --> C2["Cluster Visualizations"]
    C --> C3["Feature Overlays"]
    
    D --> D1["Gene Program Info Plots"]
    D --> D2["Enriched GP Info Plots"]
    D --> D3["Gene Importance Visualizations"]
    
    E --> E1["Communication Network Plots"]
    E --> E2["Cell Type Chord Plots"]
    E --> E3["GP Communication Matrices"]
    
    subgraph "External Libraries"
        F1["Matplotlib"]
        F2["Scanpy (sc.pl)"]
        F3["Squidpy (sq.pl)"]
        F4["Seaborn"]
        F5["NetworkX"]
    end
    
    B1 & B2 & B3 --> F2 & F3
    C1 & C2 & C3 --> F2
    D1 & D2 & D3 --> F1 & F2
    E1 & E2 & E3 --> F1 & F5
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb]()

## Spatial Data Visualization

Spatial visualizations in NicheCompass enable the display of data in the physical coordinates of the sample. These visualizations help identify spatial patterns of gene expression, cell types, and gene program activities.

### Spatial Cell Type Visualization

The most basic spatial visualization displays cell types or clusters in physical space:

```python
# Visualize cell-level annotated data in physical space
sc.pl.spatial(adata,
              color=cell_type_key,
              palette=cell_type_colors,
              spot_size=spot_size)
```

### Spatial Gene Program Activity Visualization

Gene program activities can be visualized in spatial coordinates to reveal spatial patterns of gene program activation:

```python
# Visualize gene program activities in physical space
sc.pl.spatial(adata=adata,
              color=gp_name,
              color_map="RdBu",
              spot_size=spot_size,
              title=f"{gp_name}: Gene Program Activity",
              colorbar_loc="bottom")
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:515-522](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:748-753]()

## Latent Space Visualization

NicheCompass creates interpretable latent representations of cells or spots. These embeddings can be visualized using dimensionality reduction techniques like UMAP to reveal relationships and patterns that may not be apparent in physical space.

### UMAP Embeddings

After training a NicheCompass model, UMAP embeddings can be generated and visualized:

```python
# Compute latent neighbor graph
sc.pp.neighbors(model.adata,
                use_rep=latent_key,
                key_added=latent_key)

# Compute UMAP embedding
sc.tl.umap(model.adata,
           neighbors_key=latent_key)

# Visualize UMAP embedding
sc.pl.umap(model.adata,
           color=cell_type_key,
           palette=cell_type_colors)
```

### Latent Space Clustering

Clustering can be performed on the latent representation to identify cell niches:

```python
# Perform Leiden clustering on latent representation
sc.tl.leiden(model.adata,
             resolution=latent_leiden_resolution,
             key_added=latent_cluster_key,
             neighbors_key=latent_key)

# Visualize clusters in latent space
sc.pl.umap(model.adata,
           color=latent_cluster_key)
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:589-597](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:823-831]()

## Gene Program Visualization

NicheCompass includes specialized tools for visualizing gene programs, their activities, and importance scores. These visualizations help interpret the biological meaning of gene programs and their roles in cell niches.

### Gene Program Info Plots

The `generate_enriched_gp_info_plots` function creates comprehensive visualizations of gene programs, showing their enrichment in specific categories, activities, and the expression patterns of top genes:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"] --> B["Collect GP Information"]
    B --> C["Compute GP Gene Importances"]
    B --> D["Compute GP Peak Importances\n(if multimodal)"]
    C --> E["Identify Top Genes"]
    D --> F["Identify Top Peaks"]
    E & F --> G["Create Visualization for Each Feature Space"]
    G --> H1["UMAP Visualizations\n(if latent feature space)"]
    G --> H2["Spatial Visualizations\n(if physical feature space)"]
    
    H1 --> I1["Enriched GP Category\nPlot"]
    H1 --> I2["GP Activity Score\nPlot"]
    H1 --> I3["Top Gene/Peak\nExpression Plots"]
    
    H2 --> J1["Enriched GP Category\nSpatial Plot"]
    H2 --> J2["GP Activity Score\nSpatial Plot"]
    H2 --> J3["Top Gene/Peak\nSpatial Expression Plots"]
```

The resulting plots include:
1. The enriched category visualization
2. Gene program activity scores
3. Expression patterns of top source and target genes
4. Expression patterns of top source and target peaks (for multimodal data)

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:212-405](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:1107-1120]()

### Example Usage

```python
# Generate enriched GP info plots
generate_enriched_gp_info_plots(
    plot_label="cell_type_enriched",
    model=model,
    sample_key=sample_key,
    differential_gp_test_results_key=differential_gp_test_results_key,
    cat_key=cell_type_key,
    cat_palette=cell_type_colors,
    n_top_enriched_gp_start_idx=0,
    n_top_enriched_gp_end_idx=10,
    feature_spaces=["latent", "batch1"],
    n_top_genes_per_gp=3,
    n_top_peaks_per_gp=0,
    scale_omics_ft=False,
    save_figs=True,
    figure_folder_path=figure_folder_path,
    file_format="png",
    spot_size=spot_size)
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](), [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:212-277]()

## Cell-Cell Communication Visualization

NicheCompass provides tools for visualizing cell-cell communication patterns based on gene program activities and spatial relationships.

### Communication Network Visualization

The `compute_communication_gp_network` and `visualize_communication_gp_network` functions enable the computation and visualization of cell-cell communication networks:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A["compute_communication_gp_network()"] --> B["Calculate Communication Scores"]
    B --> C["Create Network Graph"]
    C --> D["visualize_communication_gp_network()"]
    
    subgraph "Network Components"
        E["Node: Cell Type"]
        F["Edge: Communication Score"]
        G["Edge Width: Strength of Communication"]
        H["Node Size: Number of Cells"]
    end
    
    D --> E & F & G & H
    
    subgraph "Layout Options"
        I["Spring Layout"]
        J["Circular Layout"]
        K["Spectral Layout"]
    end
    
    D --> I & J & K
```

### Cell Type Chord Plots

The `create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df` function creates chord diagrams to visualize interactions between cell types:

```python
# Create cell type chord plot
create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df(
    adata=model.adata,
    df=cell_type_agg_df,
    link_threshold=0.01,
    cell_type_key=cell_type_key,
    group_key=sample_key,
    groups="all",
    plot_label="Cell-Cell Communication",
    save_fig=True,
    file_path=f"{figure_folder_path}/cell_type_chord_plot.png")
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:105-210](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb]()

## Multimodal Data Visualization

For multimodal analyses (e.g., combined RNA-seq and ATAC-seq), NicheCompass provides tools to visualize relationships between different modalities.

### RNA and ATAC Correlation Visualization

When working with multimodal data, correlations between RNA expression and chromatin accessibility can be visualized:

```python
# Visualize correlation between RNA expression and chromatin accessibility
generate_enriched_gp_info_plots(
    plot_label="multimodal_analysis",
    model=model,
    sample_key=sample_key,
    differential_gp_test_results_key=differential_gp_test_results_key,
    cat_key=cell_type_key,
    cat_palette=cell_type_colors,
    n_top_enriched_gp_start_idx=0,
    n_top_enriched_gp_end_idx=5,
    feature_spaces=["latent"],
    n_top_genes_per_gp=2,
    n_top_peaks_per_gp=2,
    scale_omics_ft=True)
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](), [src/nichecompass/utils/analysis.py:286-295]()

## Customization and Best Practices

### Color Customization

NicheCompass provides a default color dictionary but also allows custom color palettes:

```python
# Create custom color dictionary for cell types
cell_type_colors = create_new_color_dict(
    adata=model.adata,
    cat_key=cell_type_key)
```

### Save Figure Configurations

Most visualization functions accept parameters for saving figures:

```python
# Common parameters for saving figures
save_figs = True
figure_folder_path = f"../figures/{current_timestamp}"
file_format = "png"
```

### Visualization Best Practices

1. **Spatial Resolution**: Adjust `spot_size` based on your data's spatial resolution (smaller for single-cell, larger for spot-based)
2. **Feature Selection**: Limit the number of features (genes/peaks) to display for clearer visualizations
3. **Consistent Color Schemes**: Use the same color scheme across different visualizations for consistency
4. **Multiple Feature Spaces**: Generate visualizations in both latent and physical spaces for comprehensive interpretation
5. **Clear Titles and Labels**: Use informative titles and labels to make visualizations self-explanatory

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb:732-735](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb:502-504]()

## Integration with Other Analysis Tools

NicheCompass visualization tools are designed to work seamlessly with analysis results, enabling the direct visualization of:

1. Differential gene program testing results
2. Cell-cell communication networks
3. Spatial reference mapping results
4. Sample integration analyses

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["NicheCompass Model"] --> B["Differential GP Testing"]
    A --> C["Cell-Cell Communication Analysis"]
    A --> D["Spatial Reference Mapping"]
    A --> E["Sample Integration"]
    
    B --> F["Visualization Tools"]
    C --> F
    D --> F
    E --> F
    
    F --> G1["generate_enriched_gp_info_plots()"]
    F --> G2["visualize_communication_gp_network()"]
    F --> G3["create_cell_type_chord_plot_from_df()"]
    F --> G4["Standard Scanpy/Squidpy plots"]
    
    G1 & G2 & G3 & G4 --> H["Final Visualizations"]
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb]()

# Page: Benchmarking Tools

# Benchmarking Tools

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.readthedocs.yaml](.readthedocs.yaml)
- [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md)

- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb)
- [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb)
- [environment.yaml](environment.yaml)
- [src/nichecompass/__init__.py](src/nichecompass/__init__.py)
- [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py](src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py)
- [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py](src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py)
- [src/nichecompass/data/__init__.py](src/nichecompass/data/__init__.py)
- [src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py](src/nichecompass/models/nichecompass.py)
- [src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py](src/nichecompass/train/trainer.py)
- [src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py](src/nichecompass/utils/__init__.py)
- [src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py](src/nichecompass/utils/gene_programs.py)
- [src/nichecompass/utils/utils.py](src/nichecompass/utils/utils.py)

</details>



The NicheCompass benchmarking tools provide quantitative metrics to evaluate how well the model preserves spatial structures and biological relationships in its latent representations. These tools are essential for assessing model performance, comparing different model configurations, and validating results across various spatial multi-omics analysis workflows.

## Overview of Benchmarking Metrics

NicheCompass includes several specialized metrics to evaluate different aspects of spatial structure preservation:

| Metric | Description | Range | Interpretation |
|--------|-------------|-------|----------------|
| CLISIS | Cell Type Local Inverse Simpson's Index Similarity - measures preservation of local neighborhood cell type heterogeneity | 0-1 | Higher is better |
| CAS | Cell type Adjacency Score - evaluates preservation of cell type adjacency patterns | 0-1 | Higher is better |
| GCS | Graph Connectivity Score - assesses preservation of global graph structure | 0-1 | Higher is better |
| NASW | Neighborhood Annotation Similarity Welch - measures similarity of neighborhood annotations | 0-1 | Higher is better |
| MLAMI | Mutual Local Ancestry Membership Index - evaluates preservation using mutual information | 0-1 | Higher is better |

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py]()

## Benchmarking Module Architecture

The benchmarking tools are organized as a dedicated module within the NicheCompass package:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NicheCompass Package"] --> B["Benchmarking Module"]
    B --> C["compute_clisis()"]
    B --> D["compute_cas()"]
    B --> E["compute_gcs()"]
    B --> F["compute_nasw()"]
    B --> G["compute_mlami()"]
    B --> H["compute_benchmarking_metrics()"]
    
    C --> I["Cell Type Local Neighborhood Preservation"]
    D --> J["Cell Type Adjacency Pattern Preservation"]
    E --> K["Global Graph Structure Preservation"]
    F --> L["Neighborhood Annotation Similarity"]
    G --> M["Mutual Information-based Assessment"]
    
    I & J & K & L & M --> N["Comprehensive Model Evaluation"]
    H --> N
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py](), [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py]()

## CLISIS: Cell Type Local Inverse Simpson's Index Similarity

The CLISIS metric is particularly important for evaluating how well a model preserves local cellular neighborhoods.

### Implementation Details

CLISIS measures how accurately the latent nearest neighbor graph preserves local neighborhood cell type heterogeneity from the spatial nearest neighbor graph. It is implemented in [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py]() and computes:

1. The Cell Type Local Inverse Simpson's Index (CLISI) for both spatial and latent representations
2. The similarity between these indices normalized to a value between 0 and 1

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["AnnData Object"] --> B["Spatial Coordinates"]
    A --> C["Latent Representation"]
    A --> D["Cell Type Annotations"]
    
    B --> E["Spatial Nearest Neighbor Graph"]
    C --> F["Latent Nearest Neighbor Graph"]
    
    E & D --> G["Spatial CLISI Scores"]
    F & D --> H["Latent CLISI Scores"]
    
    G & H --> I["Compute Normalized Similarity"]
    I --> J["CLISIS Score (0-1)"]
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py:18-216]()

The CLISIS implementation supports:
- Using precomputed nearest neighbor graphs or computing them on the fly
- Single-batch and multi-batch analyses
- Parallel computation with the `n_jobs` parameter

The CLISI itself measures the effective number of different cell types in each cell's local neighborhood, with higher values indicating more diverse neighborhoods.

## Using Benchmarking Tools

### Basic Usage

Each metric can be calculated individually:

```python
from nichecompass.benchmarking import compute_clisis, compute_cas, compute_gcs

# Compute CLISIS metric
clisis_score = compute_clisis(
    adata, 
    cell_type_key='cell_type', 
    latent_key='nichecompass_latent'
)

# Compute CAS metric
cas_score = compute_cas(
    adata, 
    cell_type_key='cell_type', 
    latent_key='nichecompass_latent'
)
```

### Computing All Metrics

You can calculate multiple metrics at once using the comprehensive evaluation function:

```python
from nichecompass.benchmarking import compute_benchmarking_metrics

metrics = compute_benchmarking_metrics(
    adata, 
    cell_type_key='cell_type', 
    latent_key='nichecompass_latent'
)
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py:8-14]()

## Benchmarking Across Different Use Cases

Different benchmarking metrics are particularly useful for specific NicheCompass use cases:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["NicheCompass Use Cases"] --> B["Single Sample Analysis"]
    A --> C["Sample Integration"]
    A --> D["Spatial Reference Mapping"]
    A --> E["Multimodal Analysis"]
    
    B --> F["Local Structure: CLISIS, NASW"]
    B --> G["Global Structure: CAS, GCS"]
    
    C --> H["Cross-sample Integration: MLAMI"]
    C --> I["Preservation of Sample-specific Structure: CLISIS, GCS"]
    
    D --> J["Reference-Query Alignment: CLISIS, CAS"]
    D --> K["Anatomical Correspondence: NASW"]
    
    E --> L["Modality Contribution: MLAMI"]
    E --> M["Multimodal Structure Preservation: CLISIS, GCS"]
    
    F & G & H & I & J & K & L & M --> N["Comprehensive Model Evaluation"]
```

Sources: [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_brain_multimodal.ipynb](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_single_sample.ipynb](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_spatial_reference_mapping.ipynb](), [docs/tutorials/notebooks/mouse_cns_sample_integration.ipynb]()

### Single Sample Analysis
In single sample analysis, benchmarking metrics evaluate how well the model captures spatial relationships within a single tissue section. CLISIS is particularly useful for assessing preservation of local cellular neighborhoods.

### Sample Integration
For sample integration, benchmarking metrics assess whether spatial characteristics are preserved while enabling meaningful comparison across samples.

### Spatial Reference Mapping
In spatial reference mapping, benchmarking tools evaluate how accurately spatial relationships are maintained when mapping query samples to reference space.

### Multimodal Analysis
For multimodal analysis (e.g., RNA-seq and ATAC-seq integration), benchmarking tools assess whether the integration preserves or enhances spatial structure representation.

## Relationship to Spatial Properties

The benchmarking metrics in NicheCompass are designed to evaluate different aspects of spatial structure preservation:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Spatial Properties to Preserve"] --> B["Local Structure"]
    A --> C["Global Structure"]
    
    B --> D["CLISIS: Local Cell Type Heterogeneity"]
    B --> E["NASW: Neighborhood Annotation Similarity"]
    
    C --> F["CAS: Cell Type Adjacency Patterns"]
    C --> G["GCS: Graph Connectivity Structure"]
    
    B & C --> H["MLAMI: Mutual Information Assessment"]
    
    D & E & F & G & H --> I["Comprehensive Spatial Structure Evaluation"]
```

Sources: [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/clisis.py](), [src/nichecompass/benchmarking/__init__.py]()

## Conclusion

The benchmarking tools in NicheCompass provide a robust framework for evaluating how well models preserve various aspects of spatial structure. By using these metrics, researchers can select optimal models and parameters for their specific spatial multi-omics analysis tasks and ensure that the biological relationships in the data are accurately represented in the model's latent space.

# API Reference

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>
